title: Murder Accused's Hand Chopped Off With Machete, Then Shot Outside Pune Court
description: The man was released from prison four days ago.
author: Yashpal Sonkamble
content:
A murder accused was attacked with a machete and then allegedly shot at while he was appearing for legal proceedings at a Pune court this afternoon.
A video of the incident showed two men repeatedly hitting the man, identified as Mandar Maruti Kiwale, with a machete outside the Shivajinagar court premises.
The accused were then seen fleeing on two scooters, while the blood-soaked man got up and tried to walk.
Multiple videos later showed him lying on a footpath with one of his hands chopped off while bystanders stood around watching.
Kiwale has been taken to a hospital, and his condition remains critical.
The police have recovered two pistols and a magazine from the spot.
According to the police, Kiwale was jailed for murdering a man, Shubham Subhash Chavan, in April 2025, in Pune's Santoshnagar Katraj over a land and financial dispute.
He was released from prison four days ago and was attacked outside the court when he arrived for legal proceedings.
Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar spoke to the Pune Police Commissioner and sought details about the incident. She has directed the police to track down the accused and take stringent action against them.

title: After BJP-Akali Alliance In Punjab, Congress Looks At Left
description: For the Congress, an understanding with CPI and CPM would be an attempt to broaden its political coalition and consolidate sections of the electorate that traditionally identify with Left politics.
author: Gurpreet Singh Chhina
content:
With the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) having already formalised their alliance ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, the Congress is exploring a possible electoral understanding with the Left parties, CPI and CPM, signalling another round of political realignments in the state.
Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh has confirmed that discussions with the Communist parties are underway and that several rounds of meetings have already taken place. Leader of Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa has also supported the possibility of an alliance, indicating that the proposal has support within the state Congress leadership.
Although the Congress has opened discussions, the contours of the proposed arrangement, particularly seat-sharing, are yet to be worked out. Pargat Singh and Bajwa have indicated that constituency distribution would be decided by taking into account the respective roles and political strengths of the parties. For now, the emphasis appears to be on exploring the possibility of an understanding before moving towards negotiations on individual seats.
The move assumes significance in the changed political landscape following the SAD-BJP reunion. The two former allies have come together again after years of political separation, bringing their respective organisational networks and support bases into a common electoral arrangement. Their alliance has also prompted other political parties to reassess their strategies ahead of the Assembly elections.
For the Congress, an understanding with CPI and CPM would be an attempt to broaden its political coalition and consolidate sections of the electorate that traditionally identify with Left politics. Both Communist parties are constituents of the INDIA bloc at the national level, making a similar arrangement in Punjab an extension of the opposition partnership beyond the Lok Sabha elections.
Challenges In Congress-Left Alliance
The proposed alliance, however, comes with its own challenges. The Left parties have limited electoral representation in the Punjab Assembly, and their actual influence would need to be assessed constituency-wise. Seat-sharing could also become a contentious issue, particularly if both sides stake claims to constituencies where they have organisational presence.
The Congress will also have to address its internal leadership equations and establish coordination among its senior state leaders as it prepares for the electoral battle.
Punjab Elections 2027: The Political Battle
The political contest is taking shape around three broad formations: the ruling AAP, the SAD-BJP alliance and a possible Congress-Left understanding. Whether these arrangements translate into a consolidation of votes or remain limited to political agreements will depend on their grassroots coordination, candidate selection and constituency-level negotiations.
With the SAD and BJP having already sealed their alliance, the Congress's ongoing conversations with CPI and CPM indicate that the process of political coalition-building in Punjab has entered another phase ahead of 2027.

title: Common Admission Test 2026 On November 29: Check Paper Pattern, Exam Day Guidelines
description: CAT 2026 Exam: Registered candidates who have not yet downloaded their admit cards can download them from the CAT website using their CAT application login ID and password until November 29.
author: Rahul Kumar
content:
CAT 2026 Exam Day Key Guidelines: The Common Admission Test 2026 (CAT 2026) will be held on November 29 in three shifts across approximately 170 cities. To ensure the security of the examination, the Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) have taken additional measures, including face matching and the deployment of mobile jammers at select locations.
A mock test with sample questions to familiarise candidates with the exam format and interface has been made available on the CAT website from November 6.
CAT 2026 Admit Card
With only a few days left for the test, registered candidates who have not yet downloaded their admit cards can download them from the CAT website using their CAT application login ID and password until November 29, 2026.
Candidates must download the admit card and print it on an A4-size sheet of paper. To avoid last-minute downloading issues, candidates are advised to download the admit card and print it at least two days before the exam.
The admit card contains key details such as the test date and shift, test centre address, and application number.
CAT 2026 Paper Pattern And Test Duration
The test will be 120 minutes long and will comprise the following three sections:
Section 1: Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension
Section 2: Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning
Section 3: Quantitative Ability
According to the information bulletin, candidates will be allotted exactly 40 minutes to answer questions in each section. They will not be allowed to switch from one section to another while answering questions in a section.
A mock exam to help candidates understand the test format and interface is available on the CAT website.
CAT 2026 Exam Day Guidelines
Candidates are advised to locate their test centre and check its accessibility at least a day before the test. This will help them choose an appropriate mode of transport and reach the test centre on time on the day of the examination.
- Candidates arriving late will not be allowed to enter the test centre and will be barred from appearing for the test.
- Before leaving for the test centre, candidates must verify and carry their original photo ID proof and CAT 2026 admit card.
- PwD candidates using a scribe should carry the scribe affidavit to the test centre. A sample scribe affidavit is available on the CAT 2026 website.
- Candidates must affix their photograph in the space provided on the admit card, as required, before reaching the test centre.
- Candidates must report to the test centre at the time mentioned on their admit card. On arrival, their admit card and photo ID will be scrutinised.
CAT 2026 Frisking And Document Verification
- Candidates should check the location of their test lab on the notice board using the application number printed on their admit card.
- Before entering the exam hall, candidates will undergo frisking. If any prohibited item is found, they will be asked to remove it, and undergo frisking again.
- In case of any argument or non-cooperation with the frisking staff, candidates may be asked to leave the test centre.
- Candidates must deposit personal belongings such as mobile phones, bags, wallets, jackets, jewellery, watches, electronic gadgets, and stationery items at the entry gate.
- Jewellery and other items containing metal are not allowed.
- Only the admit card, original photo identity card, and other necessary documents will be allowed inside the test lab.
- Socks, plain pullovers, sweaters, and cardigans without pockets are allowed.
- Candidates with metal implants, pacemakers or similar medical devices should carry a medical certificate along with the authorisation letter received from the IIM.
- There is no facility for safekeeping candidates' personal belongings outside the test lab. The test-conducting authority will not be responsible for any damage to or loss of such belongings.
- After frisking, candidates will proceed for document verification.
- The candidate's admit card with the affixed photograph, original photo identity proof and other required documents, if any, will be checked at the document verification desk.
- Candidates must carry any one of the original and valid government-issued photo identity documents along with the admit card: PAN card, Driving licence, Voter ID, Passport, Aadhaar card with photograph, E-Aadhaar, Ration card, other valid government-issued identification documents, where applicable.
- The photo identity proof must not be damaged or smudged.
- Candidates using a scribe must carry the scribe affidavit. Candidates with a pacemaker, metal implant or other medical device should carry the required medical certificate and authorisation letter.
- After successful document verification, candidates will be allowed to proceed to their respective test lab.
- Candidates are advised to take a bio break, if required, before entering the test lab.
CAT 2026 Registration And Biometric Verification
- After document verification, candidates will proceed to the registration desk.
- During registration, photograph and iris capture will be mandatory for all candidates. This will be followed by signing the attendance sheet.
- Candidates must ensure that there is no discrepancy in their signature on the attendance sheet, as it will be verified against the admit card and original photo identity proof.
- A scribble pad and pen will be provided for rough work. Candidates must mention their name and application number on the scribble pad provided to them.
CAT 2026 Computer-Based Test Instructions
- After entering the test lab, candidates will not be allowed to leave before the test ends unless a medical emergency arises.
- The exam lab invigilator will read out the instructions before the test begins. Candidates attempting to appear for the test more than once may face action as per the prescribed rules.
- Candidates must use the mouse to mark answers or the on-screen keyboard to answer non-MCQ questions. They must not use the physical keyboard at any point, as doing so will lock the computer system.
- Candidates must not disturb others. They will not be allowed to take a bio break unless there is a medical emergency. If a candidate takes a bio break for any reason, re-frisking will be conducted.
- Any time lost due to a bio break and re-frisking will not be compensated.
- The exam lab invigilator will instruct candidates to log in to the test screen. Candidates must use the mouse on their allocated system to log in and click the keyboard icon on the screen to use the virtual keyboard.
- After logging in, candidates must verify their profile information. If the details are correct, they should click the confirmation icon to proceed.
- The next screen will display the test-related instructions. Candidates should read the instructions carefully and click 'Next' to proceed.
- Candidates must then read and agree to the declaration by selecting the checkbox. The 'I am ready to begin' button will then be enabled. Candidates should click the button to start the test.
CAT 2026 Marking Scheme And Calculator Rules
- The computer mouse must be used to answer questions. Using the physical keyboard will lock the computer system.
- The test will comprise multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and non-MCQ questions.
- Unattempted questions will receive zero marks. For MCQs, an incorrect answer will result in a deduction of one mark. There will be no negative marking for non-MCQ questions.
- A virtual keyboard will be displayed on the screen for answering non-MCQ questions. Candidates must use the mouse to operate it.
- The use of an external or physical calculator is not allowed. However, candidates can use the on-screen calculator available on the test screen.
- Each section will be allotted 40 minutes, making the total test duration 120 minutes.
- PwD candidates will receive an additional 13 minutes and 20 seconds for each section, taking the total test duration to 160 minutes.
- The timer on the screen will display the remaining time for the section being attempted. Once 40 minutes are completed, the timer will reach zero, and the section will be locked.
- The 'Submit' button will be enabled. By clicking it, candidates will move to the next section. Otherwise, the section will be auto-submitted.
- Candidates are not allowed to leave the test lab before completing the test. PwD candidates may submit their answers for a section at any point between 40 minutes and 53 minutes and 20 seconds. Therefore, a PwD candidate may leave the lab between 120 and 160 minutes, depending on the time taken to complete the test.
CAT 2026 Answer Review And On-Screen Options
Candidates will have the following options while answering questions:
- Save and Next: Saves the answer and takes the candidate to the next question.
- Clear Response: Clears the selected answer for the current question.
- Mark for Review and Next: Marks a question for review so that the candidate can return to it later. The question may or may not be answered.
If a question is answered and marked for review, the answer will be recorded, and the question will remain marked for review. At the end of the section, it will be considered answered.
A panel on the right-hand side of the screen will display the status of questions using different colours:
- Green: Answered and not marked for review.
- Red: Visited but neither answered nor marked for review.
- Grey: Not visited or viewed.
- Violet: Marked for review but not answered.
- Violet with a green mark: Answered and marked for review.
Candidates can also view other details, such as the question paper. They can view the entire question paper for a particular section by clicking the 'Question Paper' button at the top right corner of the screen. The Profile option allows candidates to view their profile-related information on the right side of the screen.
The Instructions option allows candidates to view the test-related instructions at any point by clicking the 'Instructions' button at the top right corner of the screen.
The Calculator option allows candidates to use the on-screen calculator.
Candidates must not tear out or retain any page from the scribble pad after the examination, as doing so may affect their candidature.
CAT 2026 Score And Result
CAT 2026 scorecards will be made available on the CAT website. Candidates may also be intimated individually through SMS.
According to the information bulletin, CAT 2026 results are expected to be declared in the first week of January 2027.
The CAT 2026 score will be valid only until December 31, 2027, and will be available on the CAT website until then. After that, no queries related to the release of CAT 2026 scorecards will be entertained.
CAT 2026 Admission Process
Each IIM is independent in setting its own eligibility criteria, including academic cut-offs and relative weightages, and follows its own selection process.
Performance in CAT 2026 is a crucial component of the selection process. IIMs may also consider candidates' previous academic performance, relevant work experience, and other factors while shortlisting candidates at various stages.
For more details, candidates can refer to the admission policies of individual IIMs on their respective websites.

title: What is Karthigai Deepam row? Why lighting a lamp has triggered a legal battle in Tamil Nadu
description: NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu government apologised before the Supreme Court on Wednesday after the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp was not lit at the
author: Ayush Pandey
content:
NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu government apologised before the Supreme Court on Wednesday after the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp was not lit at the designated Deepathoon stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai on November 24, despite the court's interim direction.In a status report filed by Madurai district collector Nishant Krishna, the state government said the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise the team proposed to carry out the ritual and instead decided to retain the customary location.The development came after the ceremonial lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple, rather than at Deepathoon, which was the subject of the Supreme Court's November 20 order. The court said it would consider the contempt plea alleging non-compliance with its directions and asked the petitioner and other parties to file appropriate applications.The dispute over the ritual's location has been continuing for years, with Hindu groups seeking permission to light the lamp at the hilltop stone pillar near the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah, while the state government and temple authorities have maintained that the customary venue is near the Ucchi Pillayar temple.
The November 24 ceremony, the subsequent explanation by the district administration and the demand for contempt proceedings have now brought the dispute back before the Supreme Court.
What is the Karthigai Deepam row?
Karthigai Deepam is a traditional Tamil Hindu festival celebrated by lighting lamps in homes and temples. At Thiruparankundram, the dispute concerns the location where the ceremonial lamp, or Maha Deepam, should be lit during the annual festival.For decades, the lamp has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes of Thiruparankundram hill. However, Hindu groups have sought permission to light it at Deepathoon, a stone pillar located higher up the hill and around 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah.The disagreement is not limited to the ritual's location. It also involves competing claims over the stone pillar's character and the hilltop's ownership and status. While Hindu groups describe Deepathoon as an ancient structure associated with the ritual, another side argues that it is a survey stone. The dargah committee has also contested the demand, claiming ownership of the hilltop.The dispute has travelled through the courts over several years. In December 2025, a single judge of the Madras High Court directed the temple authorities to light the lamp at Deepathoon. A division bench upheld the direction in its January 6, 2026, judgment. The state government subsequently challenged the High Court's decision before the Supreme Court.The Tamil Nadu government and the temple administration have maintained that the lamp has traditionally been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple. The state has also raised concerns over the legal and administrative implications of allowing the ritual at the disputed pillar, including the possibility of law-and-order complications because of its proximity to the dargah.
What did the Supreme Court order on November 20
On November 20, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi permitted the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time interim arrangement. The order came while the Supreme Court was hearing challenges to the Madras High Court's directions on the ritual.The court allowed only a restricted team authorised by the temple administration and government officials to go to the location and carry out the ceremony. It also designated the district collector as the nodal officer responsible for coordination and supervision.The Supreme Court imposed safeguards to prevent any escalation at the disputed site. It restrained members of the public from going to the location and prohibited processions, public gatherings, slogan-raising and demonstrations during the ceremony. The court also stayed portions of the Madras High Court judgment that had upheld the direction to restore the practice of lighting the lamp at Deepathoon.Importantly, the permission was limited to November 24 and did not settle the larger dispute over the ritual's history, the hilltop's ownership, or any customary or religious right to light the lamp at the pillar. The court clarified that neither the permission nor the ceremony could be treated as proof of an established custom or a continuing right of access to the location.The Tamil Nadu government subsequently approached the Supreme Court seeking a review of the November 20 order and a stay on the one-time permission. However, the interim direction remained the basis for the November 24 arrangements.
What happened on November 24
The Karthigai Deepam ceremony took place amid heightened security and tension at Thiruparankundram on November 24. However, the lamp was not lit at Deepathoon, the location specified by the Supreme Court. Instead, the Maha Deepam was lit at the customary Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple at around 6 pm.The development came hours after Madurai collector Nishant Krishna told the Madurai bench of the Madras High Court that the Supreme Court's directions would be implemented. The High Court had also reminded officials of their responsibility to comply with the apex court's order and warned of contempt proceedings in the event of non-compliance.State law minister C T R Nirmalkumar confirmed the lighting at the customary location in a post on X, saying: "Karthigai Mahadeepam has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near Ucchi Pillaiyar temple, directly above the sanctum sanctorum of the presiding deity at Thiruparankundram".The decision triggered protests by Hindu organisations and BJP workers, who demanded that the government implement the Supreme Court's direction. Tensions were reported near the hill, where protesters raised slogans against the state government. Police had deployed more than 5,600 personnel in Thiruparankundram and adjoining areas, with restrictions imposed on public access to the hilltop.The district administration later said that the last-minute decision to retain the customary venue followed concerns raised by the temple's Board of Trustees. The trustees maintained that the Deepa Mandapam was the traditional location for the ritual and that the practice should continue there.
Why did the Madurai collector say the lamp could not be lit at Deepathoon
In a status report filed before the Supreme Court, Madurai district collector Nishant Krishna said the administration had made arrangements to implement the November 20 order but could not proceed because the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise the team proposed to light the lamp.According to the district administration's explanation, the Supreme Court had designated the collector as the coordinating officer, while the temple administration was responsible for authorising the personnel who would carry out the ritual. The administration said it had completed the necessary arrangements, but the trustees eventually resolved to retain the customary location.The Board of Trustees cited religious traditions and established worship practices in support of its decision. It maintained that the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple was the customary venue and that the location was directly above the head of Lord Murugan, the presiding deity. The trustees also referred to Agama rules governing temple rituals and festivals.In its statement after the ceremony, the district administration said: "The trustees unanimously resolved to retain the customary venue, citing religious traditions and established worship practices."The trustees said their decision followed an examination of historical and religious records and consultations with the temple's Sthanikars, or hereditary ritual functionaries. They also decided to place their findings before the court.The collector apologised for the failure to light the lamp at Deepathoon and maintained that the administration had made every effort to comply with the Supreme Court's direction. The state's position was that the district administration could not independently authorise another team to perform the ritual in the absence of the temple Board of Trustees' approval.The status report also maintained that there had been no wilful or deliberate disobedience of the Supreme Court's directions. The government said the failure to carry out the ceremony at the designated location was due to the trustees' decision to retain the customary venue.
What is the contempt plea against Tamil Nadu officials
The failure to light the lamp at Deepathoon led to demands for contempt proceedings against the state authorities. The petitioner seeking permission for the ritual alleged that the government had failed to comply with the Supreme Court's November 20 direction despite assurances given before the Madras High Court that the order would be implemented.During Wednesday's proceedings, a senior advocate appearing for the petitioner termed the developments "most unfortunate". He argued that the flame should have been carried to Deepathoon and the lamp lit there, and alleged deliberate non-compliance with the apex court's directions.The counsel also urged the Supreme Court to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings against the authorities concerned. When the senior advocate indicated that the petitioners would move a contempt plea, the bench said, "File it, and then we will see."The Supreme Court asked the petitioner and other parties to file appropriate applications and said it would hear the matter. The bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi also said it would peruse the status report filed by the state government.The contempt allegation centres on whether the authorities failed to implement the Supreme Court's specific direction despite the district administration being tasked with coordinating the ceremony. The state government, however, has denied wilful disobedience and attributed the failure to the temple trustees' decision not to authorise the proposed team.The Supreme Court's consideration of the contempt plea will therefore bring the conduct of the officials and the explanation submitted by the district administration under judicial scrutiny.
Opposition slams Tamil Nadu government
The failure to light the lamp at Deepathoon has triggered sharp criticism from BJP leaders, who have accused the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government of disregarding the Supreme Court's interim order and hurting the sentiments of devotees.BJP national general secretary B L Santhosh accused the state government of defying the court's directions and said the government would face a "civilisational and legal challenge". In a post on X, he alleged that the Madurai district administration had lit the lamp at the Ucchi Pillayar Mandapam instead of the Deepathoon stone pillar as directed by the Supreme Court.In another post, Santhosh accused the government of compromising the sentiments of devotees to accommodate its political allies. He said: "You people have hurt devotes & defied SC Order to please some alliance partners & you yourself is Law Minister of a Govt which will fully defied SC Order . To please some friends you let down crores of devotees," he alleged.Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran also accused the state government and district administration of failing to implement the court's order. He criticised the decision to light the lamp at the customary location after the collector had assured the Madras High Court that the Supreme Court's direction would be followed."Lighting the lamp at the Pillaiyar temple after assuring the court that arrangements were being made is an act of deception. It is akin to fooling a child with candy, and they are attempting to deceive the Supreme Court and High Court judges," Nagenthran said.
BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan also accused the government of violating the interim order and alleged that the decision was taken to appease its alliance partners. She questioned why the government had not raised its objections based on Agama rules before the Supreme Court.The BJP's criticism came alongside protests by Hindu organisations in different parts of Tamil Nadu. Demonstrations were reported in Ramanathapuram and Pollachi, where protesters demanded that the government comply with the Supreme Court's direction. Police detained protesters involved in road blockades, while cases were registered against members of BJP and Hindu organisations over the demonstrations.The state government and temple trustees, however, have defended the decision to retain the customary location, citing religious traditions and established worship practices.
Ayush Pandey is a journalist at The Times of India, covering breaking news, politics, defence, and major legal and policy developments across India and the world. His reporting focuses on elections, national security, and institutional affairs, tracking the decisions and conflicts that shape public life. He specialises in sharp explainers and in-depth feature stories that go beyond headlines to decode political shifts, defence strategy, geopolitical flashpoints, and changing public sentiment. His work combines speed, clarity, and depth for a fast-moving digital audience.

title: Had Sharad Pawar joined NDA in 2019, PM Modi may have considered him for President: Union minister Athawale
description: NEW DELHI: Union minister of state Ramdas Athawale on Wednesday said NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar could have been considered for the 2022 presidential
author: Abhishek Mishra
content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister of state Ramdas Athawale on Wednesday said NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar could have been considered for the 2022 presidential election by Prime Minister Narendra Modi had he joined the BJP-led NDA in 2019.Athawale told news agency IANS that he had repeatedly persuaded the veteran politician to join the alliance on the basis of a common minimum programme."I was the one who had suggested that Sharad Pawar should join the NDA in 2019. I repeatedly told him that we should come together on the basis of a Common Minimum Programme. From 2014 to 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi accelerated the country's development, and significant progress was made across several sectors," he said.
Athawale said Modi held Pawar in high regard and recalled that the prime minister had considered the NCP (SP) chief his ideal during his tenure as Gujarat chief minister."Prime Minister Narendra Modi believes in development, and our mission is to make India the world's number one economy by 2047. He has always held Sharad Pawar in high regard. When Modi was the chief minister of Gujarat, he used to say that he considered Pawar his ideal.
Therefore, I believe Sharad Pawar should have joined the NDA. Had he joined in 2019, perhaps Prime Minister Narendra Modi would have considered him for the 2022 presidential election," the Union minister told IANS.On seat-sharing talks between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, Athawale said the two INDIA bloc partners could struggle to reach an agreement and might even contest separately."I do not know what compromise will be reached between the two parties, but I do not think the Samajwadi Party will offer them so many seats. It is also possible that the SP and Congress may contest the elections separately. However, the decision rests with them," he said.
Commenting on the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) renewing their alliance ahead of Punjab assembly elections, Athawale said the move would strengthen the NDA's prospects in the state.Recalling the alliance's tenure under former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal, he said the two parties had remained in power for several years.Athawale also claimed that people in Punjab were increasingly dissatisfied with the Aam Aadmi Party government, citing concerns over drug trafficking, the condition of young people and farmers' issues.
Abhishek Mishra is a Digital Content Producer at The Times of India, working with the news desk. He writes with a keen eye on foreign policy, defence developments, and the shifting currents of geopolitics-and yes, Indian politics always finds a way onto his radar too.

title: Rahul Gandhi assets case: SC quashes Allahabad HC orders seeking CBI, ED inquiry
description: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside Allahabad high court orders directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement
author: Abhishek Mishra
content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside Allahabad high court orders directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to examine allegations of disproportionate assets against leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, news agency ANI reported.A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant remitted the matter to the Allahabad HC for fresh consideration.The high court had earlier directed the two central agencies to verify the allegations made against Rahul and apprise it of the progress in the matter.
It had also expressed dissatisfaction with the CBI's affidavit and sought a fresh one detailing the status of its inquiry.The petition was filed by Karnataka-based BJP worker S Vignesh Shishir, who alleged that Rahul possessed assets disproportionate to his known sources of income.He had sought a probe against Rahul and other members of his family.According to Bar and Bench, Senior advocate Kapil Sibal appeared for Rahul Gandhi in the matter.Earlier, the Supreme Court had deferred proceedings before the Allahabad HC and restrained the CBI and ED from submitting any report to it.
Abhishek Mishra is a Digital Content Producer at The Times of India, working with the news desk. He writes with a keen eye on foreign policy, defence developments, and the shifting currents of geopolitics-and yes, Indian politics always finds a way onto his radar too.

title: Thirupparankundram Deepathoon row: What does John Doe order passed by Madras HC mean?
description: Thirupparankundram Deepathoon row: What is Madras HC's John Doe order?
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, on November 24, 2026, passed a ‘John Doe’ order in the Deepathoon case with regard to the lighting of the lamp at Thirupparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai for Karthigai Deepam. The High Court bench restrained anyone from violating the November 20 Supreme Court order which allowed the lighting of the lamp on the hillock as a “limited one-time arrangement” only.
Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row LIVE
What is a John Doe order?
A ‘John Doe’ order is an ex parte injuction ordered against unknown persons. Ex parte injunctions are injunctions that are granted even without hearing the other party. Issued against anonymous offenders, these are also called ‘Ashok Kumar’ orders in India and are equivalents of the place holder ‘John Doe’ used in the U.S.
Who are John Doe orders issued against?
Often used as a prohibitory measure by the courts, John Doe orders are issued against anonymous offenders or the world at large.
In the Thirupparankundram-Deepathoon case, the High Court restricted “members of the general public” from calling for violating the November 20 order issued by the Supreme Court on the issue.
What did the court say in the Deepathoon order?
“Article 144 of the Constitution mandates that all authorities, civil and judicial, in the territory of India shall act in aid of the Supreme Court. The District Collector is a civilian authority and Article 144 will squarely apply to him. Since officials brazenly defied judicial orders last year in connection with Karthigai Deepam, we deem it necessary to remind the District Collector that he is a public servant who is answerable only to the Supreme Court in this case. He shall ignore any contra advice given by any other authority,” the Bench said.
“We are sure that no law officer worth his salt will counsel him to act in contravention of the order dated November 20. No doubt, a review petition has been filed before the Supreme Court in respect of the order dated November 20. But no order has been passed in the review petition...The law that has been laid down is that pendency of a review petition is not a ground for non-compliance,” the court added.
Frequently used in intellectual property right cases
John Doe or Ashok Kumar orders are frequently used in intellectual property right cases.
A 2021 report published in The Hindu notes that there has been a rise in John Doe orders as a “pre-emptive measure against copyright infringement.”
A 2026 report in The Hindu notes that actor Salman Khan had “sought an injunction against unknown persons, joined as Defendant No. 1 (’John Doe’ or ‘Ashok Kumar’) in a case relating to a China-based AI voice generation platform seeking to vacate an interim injunction protecting Mr Khan’s personality rights.
What is the Thirupparankundram Deepathoon issue?
The controversy revolves around the Thirupparankanduram hillock in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai and the lighting of a ceremonial lamp on the day of Karthigai Deepam.
On November 20, the Supreme Court had ruled allowing the lighting of the lamp on the deepathoon atop the Thirupparankundram Hill as a “limited one-time arrangement.” The deepathoon, or stone lamp pillar, is around 50 metres from the Sikandar Badusha Dargah. While the dargah is on the hilltop, the Subramaniya Swamy Temple is at the base of the hillock. The court’s interim arrangement comes amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the dargah on the ownership of the hilltop and the deepathoon site.
However, the ruling TVK government on November 24, defied the Supreme Court order, and the festival lamp was lit only at its customary place at the Thirupparankundram hill.

title: Supreme Court sets aside Allahabad High Court order for CBI, ED enquiries into DA complaint against Rahul Gandhi
description: Supreme Court halts CBI/ED probe orders against Rahul Gandhi, requires his party impleadment and sends case back to High Court.
author: Krishnadas Rajagopal
content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) set aside orders passed by the Allahabad High Court directing Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and Enforcement Directorate (ED) inquiries into a disproportionate assets’ complaint against Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.
Mr. Gandhi had challenged the interim orders as a green signal to conduct a “fishing” expedition against him. The Congress leader had submitted in his appeal to the Supreme Court that the interim orders were passed without making him a party or hearing him first.
A three-judge bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant directed that Mr. Gandhi be impleaded as a party, while relegating the case back to the High Court to be heard from the very threshold.
“We are on the basic fundamentals of hearing. We will not make any observations on the merits of the case,” Chief Justice Kant said.
The complainant, Vignesh Shishir, who is the respondent before the Supreme Court in Mr. Gandhi’s appeal, said that an accused does not have an inherent right to be heard during the pre-FIR stage.
However, Justice Joymalya Bagchi pointed out that under the new law, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the scope for the accused to be heard has been expanded.
Mr. Gandhi, represented by advocate Prasanna S., termed the series of directions passed by the Lucknow Bench of the High Court in May and July directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) to probe the allegations against him as one of the rarest instances of a constitutional court acting contrary to several first principles or basic, fundamental legal rules all at once.
The Opposition Leader had termed these orders “outside the settled rules of law or erroneous, which would be a gross understatement.”
Mr. Gandhi submitted that the proceedings were characterised by the unjustified secrecy of in-chamber hearings, with documents and pleadings kept under wraps in sealed covers.
He had maintained that the High Court did not refer to the foundational material or provide reasons in the orders for directing a “roving inquiry”.
Mr. Gandhi said the High Court did not consider the fact that Mr. Shishir is a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Rashtriya Swayam Sevak Sangh (RSS), who had filed multiple complaints and public-interest litigation against him in the past, including allegations of foreign citizenship, up to now, and allegations of holding disproportionate assets.
Mr. Gandhi had said that the repeated filing of proceedings against him by the same “motivated individuals”, based on “unsubstantiated allegations”, constituted a relevant background demonstrating a pattern of persistent and vexatious litigation.

title: Nazir Ahmad Wani: Kashmiri terrorist who joined Indian Army and died fighting terrorists
description: Once involved in militancy in Kashmir Nazir Ahmad Wani joined the Indian Army and became a hero He was killed fighting terrorists in Shopian in 2018 Eight years later his remarkable journey from terrorist to soldier and Ashok Chakra awardee remains a story worth telling
author: Anand Singh
content:
Nazir Ahmad Wani: Kashmiri terrorist who joined Indian Army and died fighting terrorists
Once involved in militancy in Kashmir, Nazir Ahmad Wani joined the Indian Army and became a hero. He was killed fighting terrorists in Shopian in 2018. Eight years later, his remarkable journey from terrorist to soldier and Ashok Chakra awardee remains a story worth telling.
Nazir Ahmad Wani was once a terrorist in Kashmir, on the other side of the Indian Army's guns in the Valley. But he later wore the Olive Greens, and died fighting terrorists for India. It was on this day, eight years ago, that Lance Naik Nazir Ahmad Wani, made the supreme sacrifice.
Wani's journey from being a militant to a soldier and national hero is one of the rarest stories of transformation.
On November 26, 2018, the body of Lance Naik Wani arrived at his village of Chak Ashmuji in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district, wrapped in the Indian Tricolour. Some 500 to 600 villagers gathered to bid him farewell. As his body was lowered into the grave, a 21-gun salute by the Indian Army rang out.
It was a poignant end to the life of a former militant.
The man who had once walked the path of militancy had gone on to earn two Sena Medals for gallantry before making the supreme sacrifice in an operation in Shopian on November 25, 2018. He was 38.
Posthumously, he was awarded the Ashok Chakra, India's highest peacetime gallantry award, becoming the first person from Jammu and Kashmir to receive the honour.
Eight years after his death, Wani's remarkable journey was recalled by Lieutenant General Satish Dua (Retd), the former Army Corps Commander in Srinagar, who has chronicled the soldier's life in his 2024 book, A General Reminisces: A Life Under Fire in Kashmir.
In a post on X, Dua wrote, "An incredible story of a terrorist who became a National Hero."
NAZIR AHMAD WANI'S LIFE WAS SHAPED BY KASHMIR CONFLICT
Nazir Ahmad Wani was born into the family of Sonuallah, a farmer who also ran a small dhaba. In the excerpt from his book, Dua describes how the family's limited income made it difficult to support their four sons.
Wani's childhood, however, was not defined by militancy alone.
Dua recalls three incidents from Wani's early years that left an impression on the young boy. One involved his Kashmiri Pandit schoolteacher, Pandit Shubhan Ji, who explained to his Muslim pupils how different religions had different customs and how communities had coexisted in Kashmir.
Another involved a retired soldier from his village who would narrate stories of his military service to local children. The soldier once told him, with pride in his voice, "Maine teen jung mein ladai ladi hai [I've fought in three wars]." Nazir was impressed. The young Wani, according to the book, concluded that it must be a heroic thing to be at war.
After listening to him speak about fighting wars, the young Nazir declared, "I will also fight wars when I grow up." The retired soldier laughed. Lt Gen Satish Dua (Retd) wrote in his book, "Little did he [the retired soldier] know that this young boy would one day become the recipient of the highest medal for bravery."
But the Kashmir in which Wani grew up was in the grip of militancy. As a teenager, he drifted towards militancy groups, initially running errands for them and eventually becoming involved in militancy.
But Wani was fortunate to find a way out of militancy through the Ikhwan, a counter-insurgency group made up of former militants who had switched sides and began working with the security forces in Kashmir.
WHAT WAS KASHMIR'S IKHWAN FORCE?
The Ikhwan emerged in Kashmir in the mid-1990s as a counter-insurgency initiative to bring former militants over to the government's side.
Lt Gen Satish Dua describes it as a bold experiment that paved the way for an even bigger one — "raising a Territorial Army battalion comprising surrendered militants".
The Ikhwan's members worked alongside security forces, using their local knowledge to identify militants, gather intelligence and support counter-insurgency operations. For young men like Nazir Ahmad Wani, it also offered a way out of militancy.
The programme was significant because the men involved often had an understanding of the local terrain and networks that could be useful to the security forces.
Wani subsequently joined the Army's 162 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army), also known as the Home and Hearth battalion of the Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry (JAK LI), in 2004.
His transition was not merely from one organisation to another. He went on to participate in counter-insurgency operations against the very kind of militancy with which he had once been associated.
NAZIR AHMAD WANI WON TWO SENA MEDALS FOR GALLANTRY
Wani was a decorated soldier. His military career was marked by repeated acts of gallantry. He received the Sena Medal for gallantry twice, first in 2007 and again in 2018.
His first Sena Medal came after an anti-militancy operation in his home district in January 2007, during which he eliminated four militants, according to a contemporaneous report in The Tribune.
The second came on the eve of Independence Day in 2018. He was recognised for eliminating a terrorist in close combat during an operation at Kund in Kulgam in November 2017. He had also helped apprehend two other militants alive.
He also served with Rashtriya Rifles (RR) units in Kashmir. The RR is a specialised counter-insurgency force of the Indian Army, raised in 1990 to tackle militancy in Jammu and Kashmir. It operates primarily in areas affected by insurgency.
His final operation would become the defining chapter of his military career.
OPERATION BATAGUND: WANI'S FINAL BATTLE IN SHOPIAN
On November 25, 2018, Wani was part of an operation launched by the 34th Battalion of Rashtriya Rifles after intelligence inputs indicated the presence of six heavily armed terrorists in Batagund, Shopian district.
According to his Ashok Chakra citation, Wani "insisted on being part of the assault team". His unit was tasked with blocking the likely escape route of the terrorists.
As the security forces established the cordon, the terrorists attempted to break through, firing indiscriminately and hurling grenades.
Wani held his position and eliminated a terrorist in a close-range exchange of fire. The man was subsequently identified as a district commander of the Lashkar-e-Taiba.
He then moved closer to the target house under heavy fire and lobbed grenades into a room where another terrorist was hiding. When a foreign terrorist attempted to escape through a window, Wani engaged him in hand-to-hand combat and eliminated him despite sustaining serious injuries.
The citation records that he continued engaging the remaining terrorists, injuring another before being hit again. He eventually succumbed to his injuries.
The official Ashok Chakra citation reads, "For displaying unparalleled bravery and supreme sacrifice in the line of duty," Wani was awarded the Ashok Chakra posthumously.
NAZIR AHMAD WANI: THE MAN BEHIND THE UNIFORM
Beyond the soldier and his military decorations, Wani was a husband and father of two sons, Athar and Shaid.
In an interview with PTI in January 2019, nearly two months after his death, his wife Mahajabeen recalled their relationship. The two had met at a school in South Kashmir around 15 years earlier.
"It was love at first sight. He was a great husband, always fiercely protecting us," she said.
She was at her parents' home when she received the news of his death. Wani had called her the previous evening to enquire about the family's well-being.
Mahajabeen, a teacher, said she did not cry when she learnt that her husband was no more. "I did not cry when I was told he is no more. There was an inner resolve which did not allow me to cry," she told PTI.
She recalled how Wani always encouraged people around him to be happy and help resolve others' problems. Inspired by him, she said she wanted to dedicate herself to educating children and guiding young minds towards becoming good citizens.
"He loved me so much. For me, he was my guiding light," she said.
On January 26, 2019, President Ram Nath Kovind posthumously conferred the Ashok Chakra on Wani. His wife and mother received the award on his behalf at the Republic Day celebrations in New Delhi.
Eight years after his death, Dua's tribute brings attention once again to a life that cannot be understood through a single label or phase. In his Instagram tribute on Wednesday, Dua described Wani's journey as "one of the greatest stories of redemption in the history of the Indian Army".

content:
65 foreign terrorists in Kashmir, 55 linked to Jaish and Lashkar: Sources
Of the 65 foreign terrorists, around 55 are believed to be associated with Jaish and Lashkar, while the remaining 10 are reportedly linked to smaller groups backed by major terror organisations, intelligence sources told India Today.
At least 65 foreign terrorists are believed to be active in Jammu and Kashmir, including around 55 linked to Pakistan-based terror outfits Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba, intelligence sources said.
With the number of homegrown terrorists in the Valley dropping to zero, security forces have intensified operations against foreign operatives, several of whom recently infiltrated from Pakistan to carry out attacks and revive terror networks in the region, sources told India Today.
Of the 65 foreign terrorists, around 55 are believed to be associated with Jaish and Lashkar, while the remaining 10 are reportedly linked to smaller groups backed by major terror organisations.
Security agencies have also identified several suspected local associates and are monitoring their movements and support networks, including overground workers (OGWs).
OVER 80 BASES SET UP AT ALTITUDES ABOVE 10,000 FEET
Security forces have established over 80 Temporary Operating Bases (TOBs) in Jammu and Kashmir's remote and mountainous areas, including several at altitudes exceeding 10,000 feet, to intensify operations against foreign terrorists.
Personnel from the Army, CRPF and Jammu and Kashmir Police have been deployed at these bases to maintain a sustained presence in difficult terrain and prevent terrorists from using forests and mountains as hideouts.
The strategy was introduced after the Pahalgam terror attack, with the first base established in Srinagar's Fakir Gujri area in July 2025. Similar bases were subsequently set up across sensitive mountainous regions to strengthen surveillance and counterterrorism operations.
Security agencies suspect that several terrorists are hiding in forests, mountain caves and traditional mud-and-stone shelters known as 'dhoks', which are commonly used by shepherds during summer.
Tracking them remains challenging as they avoid conventional communication channels. Security forces are relying on local intelligence inputs and informants while continuing search operations in remote areas.
LOCAL TERRORIST COUNT DROPS TO ZERO
The crackdown comes after security agencies declared the Kashmir Valley free of homegrown terrorists, with their numbers falling to zero following the recent killing of terrorist Latif in an encounter.
Around half a dozen local terrorists have been killed in counterterrorism operations over the past two years, while fresh recruitment has also stopped, dealing a blow to terror networks.

title: Gujarat coast gets maritime security boost as BSF adds over 25 interceptor boats
description: The BSF has added more than two dozen interceptor boats to step up patrols along Gujarat039s coast and respond faster to suspected infiltration smuggling and emergencies at sea
author: Jitendra Bahadur Singh
content:
Gujarat coast gets maritime security boost as BSF adds over 25 interceptor boats
The BSF has added more than two dozen interceptor boats to step up patrols along Gujarat's coast and respond faster to suspected infiltration, smuggling and emergencies at sea.
The Border Security Force (BSF) has added more than two dozen interceptor boats to its fleet to step up patrols along Gujarat’s coast and respond faster to suspected infiltration and smuggling by sea.
The new boats will help BSF crews track, pursue and stop suspicious vessels for inspection. Smugglers sometimes use fishing boats or other small vessels that can blend in with regular traffic.
Small, fast boats can also change course quickly, making them harder to track. BSF crews can coordinate with other agencies along the coast if further action is needed.
The BSF can also deploy the interceptors alongside other agencies to reach stranded fishermen, assist vessels involved in accidents and search for people reported missing at sea.
Personnel will receive hands-on training in boat handling, navigation and maintenance. Crews will practise operating in changing weather and water conditions and navigating around other vessels.
WHY GUJARAT’S COAST MATTERS
Gujarat’s coastline is home to ports and industrial centres, and its waters see regular traffic from commercial ships and fishing boats. Security agencies monitor the coast for smuggling, illegal crossings and potential attacks from the sea.
The BSF patrols stretches of the maritime frontier, including the Harami Nala area near the border with Pakistan.
Shallow waters and changing tides limit where conventional vessels can operate along parts of the coast, so the force uses boats of different sizes and capabilities.

title: Keralam govt working to resolve decades-old church dispute: CM Satheesan | India News
description: Keralam govt working to resolve decades-old church dispute: CM Satheesan | India News
author: PTI
content:
Keralam govt working to resolve decades-old church dispute: CM Satheesan
Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam Chief Minister V D Satheesan on Wednesday said his government was making efforts to resolve the decades-old dispute between the rival Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church and Jacobite Syrian Christian Church, and would adopt only a fair and just approach in dealing with the issue.
Speaking at a press conference here after the weekly Cabinet meeting, Satheesan said the dispute was not a recent development but has been continuing for several decades, and he has been trying to find an amicable settlement.
"The dispute has been there for years. I am someone who has been trying to resolve it. The issue became more intense following the visit of the Patriarch of Antioch . The government's effort is to ensure that the situation does not worsen," he said.
He said the government was trying to prevent further estrangement between the two factions and bring them closer through dialogue.
"That is the government's position. We will take only a fair and just stand. Complaints will be examined seriously and whatever can be done will be done," the CM said.
His remarks came a day after his latest effort to establish peace between the two factions faced a fresh hurdle, with the Orthodox Church leadership expressing strong resentment over recent developments involving disputed churches.
Satheesan on Tuesday visited the Malankara Orthodox Church headquarters at Devalokam in Kottayam and held discussions with its head, Catholicos Baselios Marthoma Mathews III, amid continuing tensions between the two factions over the administration of several churches.
The meeting, which lasted more than half an hour, followed objections raised by the Orthodox Church over recent visits by Moran Mor Ignatius Aphrem II, Patriarch of Antioch and supreme head of the Universal Syriac Orthodox Church, to churches at Manarcad, Kothamangalam and Rakad.
The Orthodox Church alleged that the visits violated court orders and its constitution and said the developments had deeply hurt its members.
Church officials had described Tuesday's discussions with the chief minister as cordial and said they had conveyed their grievances to him.
The dispute between the Orthodox and Jacobite factions has its roots in differences over ecclesiastical authority and the administration of churches under the Malankara Church.
While the Orthodox faction recognises the Catholicos of the East as the head of the Church in India, the Jacobite faction recognises the Patriarch of Antioch as its supreme spiritual head.
The differences have led to prolonged legal battles and disputes over the control of several churches in Keralam.
In its 2017 verdict, the Supreme Court upheld the validity of the 1934 Constitution of the Malankara Church, strengthening the Orthodox faction's position in the dispute. However, tensions have persisted in several parishes, with the implementation of court orders frequently triggering fresh confrontations.
Successive efforts to resolve the differences through negotiations have failed to achieve a lasting settlement.
Satheesan recently reiterated his intention to bring peace between the two factions and find an amicable solution to the decades-old dispute. Tuesday's meeting with the Orthodox Church leadership was part of that initiative.

title: Supreme Court sets aside Allahabad HC order directing probe into Rahul Gandhi’s assets, orders fresh hearing | India News
description: A Supreme Court bench passed the order on a petition filed by Gandhi challenging the order passed by the HC directing CBI and ED to verify the allegations. | India News
author: Abraham Thomas
content:
Supreme Court sets aside Allahabad HC order directing probe into Rahul Gandhi’s assets, orders fresh hearing
A Supreme Court bench passed the order on a petition filed by Gandhi challenging the order passed by the HC directing CBI and ED to verify the allegations.
The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside orders passed by the Allahabad high court directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to look into allegations of disproportionate assets against Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi.
A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant passed the order on a petition filed by Gandhi challenging the order passed by the high court in May directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to verify the allegations made in a petition filed by a BJP activist S Vignesh Shishir and file an affidavit detailing status of enquiry.
As Gandhi objected to the order being passed behind his back, the bench, also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, set aside the order of the HC and requested the chief justice of the Allahabad high court to constitute a new bench for the fresh commencement of hearing on the petition. The court made it clear that the hearing will be in open court even as the complainant Shishir insisted on having in-camera proceedings owing to threat to his life.
ALSO READ: 'Unable to digest': BJP takes jibe at Rahul Gandhi after India ranks 3rd on Asia Power Index
The bench further directed Shishir to make Gandhi a party in his petition and kept open all arguments on merits, including the issue of maintainability of the petition, to be argued before the high court.
Earlier on August 17, the top court had issued notice on Gandhi’s petition and directed that no report shall be submitted by CBI, ED or any other agencies as per the Allahabad high court’s order in May. The top court had further asked the high court to defer the hearing of the case till further orders.
Shishir, who was present in court, requested protection as he is a witness in the case. The bench refused to pass any order on merits. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal who appeared for Gandhi along with advocate S Prasanna raised questions on the petition’s maintainability as the same petitioner made attempts since 2024 leveling similar allegations.
ALSO READ: Rahul Gandhi says Rajiv Gandhi's security was removed ‘so that he could be killed’
While the CBI and ED had told the top court on an earlier occasion that the HC has only permitted them to make an enquiry, the bench had pointed out that if the allegations were so serious, why the agency kept quiet all this while before relying on the HC order to proceed in the matter.
The court had then said, “If there is prima facie material, our understanding of the law suggests that you can proceed as per law. But if the court wants to issue a direction, courts are expected to follow the principles of natural justice.”
Gandhi had challenged a series of orders passed by the Allahabad high court on a petition alleging that he possesses assets disproportionate to his known sources of income. He also sought transfer of proceedings from the high court. Shishir in his petition sought a probe against Gandhi and other members of his family.
The high court had in May directed CBI and ED to verify the allegations made by Shishir and on July 20 passed another order expressing dissatisfaction with the agency’s response. The high court also considered ED’s response and said that the agency had taken the required steps and was free to proceed further if its investigation yielded material warranting action.
Separately, Shishir has another petition pending before the Allahabad high court seeking criminal action against Gandhi on allegations of violations of citizenship laws. Shishir has claimed that Gandhi held a British passport in addition to his Indian passport.

title: 'Guardian, Original Advisor': West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari Credits Pranab Mukherjee For Trinamool Exit,
description: Suvendu Adhikari revealed that former President Pranab Mukherjee advised him to leave TMC and join BJP.
author: Shuddhanta Patra
content:
'Guardian, Original Advisor': West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari Credits Pranab Mukherjee For Trinamool Exit, BJP Switch
Suvendu Adhikari revealed that former President Pranab Mukherjee advised him to leave TMC and join BJP.
Ever wondered who influenced Suvendu Adhikari’s switch to the BJP and his rise to West Bengal’s top post? The Bengal Chief Minister has revealed that former President of India Pranab Mukherjee advised him to leave the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and align with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Recalling a conversation with the late Congress veteran at Rashtrapati Bhavan, Adhikari described Mukherjee as his “original advisor".
“My original advisor was later Pranab Mukherjee. I went to Raisana Hill after he became President," the West Bengal CM revealed this on Tuesday at the Economic Times Bengal Ascends summit in Kolkata.
- Suvendu Promises Prime-Time Slots For Bengali Films, Construction Of Theatres To Promote Regional Cinema
- Bengal Cinema Row: Suvendu Makes One Bengali Film Mandatory In Prime Time | News18
- 20 Years After Tata Exit, Singur Eyes Industrial Revival With Ashok Leyland Truck Plant
- West Bengal To Become 'Paschim Banga'? CM Suvendu Says Proposal To Be Tabled In Assembly | News 18
Adhikari, who was a close aide to then West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, left the TMC, and joined the BJP in 2020, months after Pranab Mukherjee’s death.
“Pranab ji told me, ‘Think about what you want to do. If you want to remain an employee, stay here. If you want to move ahead on your own, stay with Modiji,’" CM Adhikari said, recalling the former President’s advice.
What were Pranab Mukherjee’s views on Mamata-led TMC ?
According to the Bengal CM, Pranab Mukherjee viewed the TMC as a political party run by an aunt-nephew duo.
“Theirs was a single-man party, a single-woman party of bua-bhatija (aunt and nephew), and it was completely like a company, with a managing chairman and a managing director," Adhikari said, referring to Mamata Banerjee and her nephew Abhishek Banerjee.
Speaking about his decision to leave the Trinamool Congress, CM Adhikari said, “I was also there, but I did not want to remain an employee, so I left."
“He was my guardian, my adviser. Apart from politics, every Indian respects Mr Pranab Mukherjee," Adhikari said, describing Mukherjee as a guardian and adviser. He emphasised that his respect for the former President went beyond political affiliations.
CM Adhikari, however, declined to elaborate on the exact time of the meeting, saying he did not want to invite controversy around the late leader.
“I don’t want to say much about this. He is no longer with us. There could be a controversy over this. I don’t want to reveal much," he said.
Pranab Mukherjee, a veteran Congress leader, served as India’s 13th President from 2012 to 2017 and was among the party’s most prominent figures before his election to the constitutional post. He passed away in August 2020.
Quick Answers
Pranab Mukherjee advised Suvendu Adhikari to think carefully about his career, stating that if he wanted to remain an employee he should stay with the TMC, but if he wanted to progress on his own he should align with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
