title: Royal Enfield commits ₹1,000 crore to Tamil Nadu to expand its electric motorcycle operations
description: Royal Enfield will invest ₹1,000 crore in Tamil Nadu over seven years to expand its EV operations, focusing on electric motorcycle development, technology and manufacturing.
author: Vivek Dubey
content:
Royal Enfield commits ₹1,000 crore to Tamil Nadu to expand its electric motorcycle operations
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 14:55 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 14:55 IST
Royal Enfield is deepening its manufacturing roots in Tamil Nadu to scale up its electric motorcycle lineup, focusing on EV product development and innovation labs. Discover how this strategic capital infusion will shape
Royal Enfield, on Wednesday, signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Tamil Nadu government to invest ₹1,000 crore over seven years, as the motorcycle maker looks to expand its electric vehicle (EV) operations.
The proposed investment will support EV product development, technology upgrades and manufacturing capabilities in the state. The company expects the investment to create direct and indirect employment opportunities for up to 500 people.
The investment is aimed at strengthening Royal Enfield's electric mobility ecosystem, including its product development and manufacturing infrastructure.
The agreement also adds to the company's existing investments in Tamil Nadu, where it has been expanding its manufacturing and engineering operations.
B Govindarajan, Managing Director of Eicher Motors Limited and CEO of Royal Enfield, said, “Tamil Nadu has been our home and the anchor for our engineering and manufacturing for several decades.”
He added that the investment reflects the company's commitment to the state and its plans for electric mobility. Royal Enfield also said it would focus on expanding its EV capabilities while contributing to local employment and economic development.
Flying Flea base
Tamil Nadu is a key manufacturing and engineering hub for Royal Enfield's global operations. The state houses four of the company's manufacturing facilities, along with its head office and technical centre.
Royal Enfield's electric mobility brand, Flying Flea, is also supported by an EV innovation lab and manufacturing facility at Vallam Vadagal in Tamil Nadu. The latest MoU is expected to support the company's efforts to develop its electric motorcycle business.
The ₹1,000 crore EV investment follows Royal Enfield's February 2026 commitment to invest ₹958 crore in expanding production capacity at its Cheyyar facility through a brownfield project. The expansion is expected to take the company's total annual motorcycle production capacity to 2 million units.
Eicher Motors, the parent company of Royal Enfield, has previously signed investment MoUs with the Tamil Nadu government in January 2024, January 2019 and May 2012. The latest agreement adds to these commitments and reinforces the company's manufacturing presence in the state.

title: CJP leader Saurav Das moves Delhi HC after being stopped from flying to UK for Oxford event
description: The CJP leader had earlier alleged that he was stopped from boarding his 1 am flight to London on Monday, where he was invited to speak at events at Oxford, Cambridge, the London School of Economics and the University of Edinburgh.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
CJP leader Saurav Das moves Delhi HC after being stopped from flying to UK for Oxford event
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 13:28 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 13:28 IST
Immigration authorities flagged the political leader's passport without presenting a formal restraining order or official circular during his departure check. He intends to pursue academic speaking engagements across sev
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das on Wednesday approached the Delhi High Court after he was stopped at the Delhi airport from travelling to the UK, where he was scheduled to speak at an Oxford University event on the “cockroach movement”.
Das’ plea was mentioned for urgent hearing before a bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma, which said the matter would be listed on Thursday.
Das’ counsel told the court that he was stopped at the immigration counter before boarding his flight to London and that no order or Look Out Circular (LOC) was shown to him.
“I was stopped at immigration. No order was shown to me. No LOC, no prohibition by any authority from letting me travel,” his counsel submitted, adding that Das could still reach the UK by November 27.
Das had earlier alleged that he was stopped from boarding his 1 am flight to London on Monday, where he was invited to speak at events at Oxford, Cambridge, the London School of Economics and the University of Edinburgh.
In a post on X, Das said, “I have been stopped by this cowardly Modi Govt at the Delhi Airport from flying to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford.”
He alleged that the government had prevented him from travelling because it was “scared” of him speaking at prestigious institutions.
“Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions!” Das said.
Das said he was stopped during immigration and was told that his passport had been flagged. He also alleged that he had not been shown any order restricting his travel.
“Why is the government so scared of an educated youth going among educated people and having an intellectual discussion?” he said.
The CJP leader had on Tuesday alleged that he received a show-cause notice hours before his scheduled flight, seeking an explanation over alleged discrepancies in his place of birth. He said his passport was issued in 2019 after police verification and that he had travelled abroad on the same passport.

title: NSA Doval calls for closer regional security cooperation to counter challenges in Indian Ocean
description: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval stated at the Colombo Security Conclave in Male that India remains committed to deepening strategic cooperation with Indian Ocean nations to counter regional secur
author: PTI
content:
NSA Doval calls for closer regional security cooperation to counter challenges in Indian Ocean
- Published OnNov 25, 2026 | 12:56 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 25, 2026 | 12:56 IST
National Security Advisor Ajit Doval stated at the Colombo Security Conclave in Male that India remains committed to deepening strategic cooperation with Indian Ocean nations to counter regional secur
India remains committed to working closely with key Indian Ocean nations to enhance their collective capacities to deal with evolving security threats, National Security Advisor Ajit Doval said on Wednesday.
In his address at the eighth Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) in Male, Doval listed various pressing challenges facing the region and called for deeper strategic cooperation to address them.
The CSC has emerged as a key regional security grouping of Indian Ocean littoral states, comprising India, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh, and Seychelles. It has largely been focusing on maritime safety, counter-terrorism, and transnational security cooperation.
”The Colombo Security Conclave represents the intersection of our Neighborhood First outlook and the MAHASAGAR vision,” Doval said.
”We are committed to continue working closely with the CSC countries to enhance our collective capacities in dealing with the evolving serious security challenges,” he added.
Last March, during his visit to Mauritius, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the vision MAHASAGAR, or ’Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions, for India’s engagement with the Global South.
Doval said he was confident that the CSC will become an effective instrument in the Indian Ocean region to provide collective security and look after common interests.
”India has been trying to work very closely with Sri Lanka, with the Maldives and other countries, and we want to see that this cooperation is further extended,” the NSA said.
”I assure all of you that India, as one of the countries which had initiated the idea of the Colombo Security Conclave, will give its best and will try to give all necessary help, assistance. I assure you of our fullest commitment to achieve our common objectives,” Doval added.
The Colombo Security Conclave was established in 2020 when India, Sri Lanka and Maldives agreed to expand the scope and membership of their trilateral meeting on maritime cooperation.
Cooperation under the CSC focuses on the five pillars of maritime safety and security, countering terrorism and radicalisation, combating trafficking and transnational organised crime and cyber security, protection of critical infrastructure, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.

title: नशा तस्करी का विरोध, जान पर आई आफत: ATM जा रहे AAP सरपंच के पति पर दिनदहाड़े फायरिंग; पैर में गोली लगने से घायल
description: पंजाब के तरनतारन में एक महिला सरपंच और उसके पति पर हमला हुआ है. आरोप है कि सरपंच का परिवार नशे के खिलाफ मुहिम चला रहा था और गांव के ही कुछ लोगों को नशा बेचने से रोका था.
author: अभिनव त्रिपाठी
content:
पंजाब के तरतारन से एक हैरान करने वाला मामला सामने आया है. यहां पर नशा के खिलाफ आवाज उठाने वालों की सुरक्षा पर फिर से सवाल खड़े हो रहे हैं. हालिया मामला खडूर साहिब विधानसभा क्षेत्र के गांव डालेके के मोड़ पर दिनदहाड़े फायरिंग की घटना ने लोगों को डरा दिया है. जानकारी के अनुसार, यहां पर आम आदमी पार्टी से जुड़ी महिला सरपंच मंजीत कौर के पति सुखबीर सिंह पर हमलावरों ने गोली चला दी.
हालांकि, गनीमत रही कि होली सुखबीर सिंह को छूकर निकल गई, जिससे वह जख्मी हो गए. उनको उपचार के लिए अस्पताल में भर्ती कराया गया, जहां से उन्हें छुट्टी मिल गई है. इस घटना को लेकर महिला सरपंच ने बताया कि वह अपने पति के साथ एटीएम जा रही थी. इसी दौरान कुछ बदमाशों ने उनकी बाइक को टक्कर मार दी.
फिर आरोपियों ने उनकी बाइक पर गोली चलाई और फिर हाथापाई शुरू कर दी. सरपंच ने कहा कि हमलावरों ने उनका मोबाइल भी छीन लिय, जिससे वह किसी को मदद के लिए न बुला पाएं. इसके बाद आरोपियों ने फिर से फायरिंग की, जिसमें सुखबीर सिंह गंभीर रूप से जख्मी हो गए. वहीं, हमलावर मौके से फरार हो गए.
घटना को लेकर महिला सरपंच मंजीत कौर ने आरोप लगाया कि गांव में कुछ लोग नशे का कारोबार करके हैं, जिसका वो और उनका परिवार काफी विरोध करता है. सरपंच ने कहा कि हमने पहले भी इस युवक को नशा बेचने से रोका था, जिस कारण परिवार को धमकियां मिल रही थी. अब उनके पति पर जानलेवा हमला हुआ है.
सरपंच का कहना है कि इसी रंजिश के कारण उनके पति को निशाना बनाया गया है. इसके अलावा उन्होंने पुलिस पर भी देरी से पहुंचने का आरोप लगाया. महिला सरपंच ने आरोपियों की जल्दी से गिरफ्तारी और सख्त कार्रवाई की मांग की है. बताया जा रहा है कि इस मामले में पुलिस ने बताया कि गोली लगने के कारण शख्स को गहरा घाव नहीं आया है और मामूली खरोंच आई हैं.
तरनतारन के एसएसपी ने बताया कि दोनों गुटों के बीच काफी पुरानी रंजिश है. पुलिस का कहना है कि सरपंच के पति पर हमला करने के मामले की जांच की जा रही है. मामले में 2 संदिग्धों की तलाश कर ली गई है और इनका आपराधिक रिकॉर्ड भी सामने आया है.

title: LoC पर हलचलः कठुआ में मिला 'टॉय एयरप्लेन', संदिग्ध गुब्बारे से भेजा गया सीक्रेट संदेश! सुरक्षा एजेंसियां चौकन्ना
description: कठुआ सेक्टर में एक संदिग्ध गुब्बारा पाया गया है. एयरप्लेन के आकार वाले इस खिलौने में PIA लिखा होने से हड़कंप मच गया. सूचना मिलने के बाद पुलिस के जवान मौके पर पहुंचे और संदिग्ध गुब्बारे को अपने कब्जे में ले लिया. पुलिस अब इसकी जांच कर रही है.
author: राज मिश्रा
content:
लश्कर आतंकी लतीफ अहमद भट्ट के मारे जाने के बाद केंद्रीय गृहमंत्री अमित शाह ने घाटी से आतंकवाद का नामो-निशान मिट जाने का दावा किया था. हालांकि, सुरक्षा बलों और विभिन्न रिपोर्टों के अनुसार आतंकी नेटवर्क की चुनौती अभी पूरी तरह समाप्त नहीं हुई है. सुरक्षाबलों के मुताबिक, पाकिस्तान के कब्जे वाले कश्मीर में फिर से आतंकी कैंप सक्रिय हैं और वहां से सीमा पार से करीब 500 आतंकी घाटी में घुसने की फिराक में हैं. इस इनपुट के बीच अब कठुआ सेक्टर में एक संदिग्ध गुब्बारा पाया गया है. एयरप्लेन के आकार वाले इस खिलौने में PIA लिखा होने से हड़कंप मच गया. सुरक्षाबलों ने तुरंत गुब्बारे को अपने कब्जे में लेकर इस सीक्रेट मैसेज को डिकोड करना शुरू कर दिया है.
गुब्बारे पर PIA लिखा होने से हड़कंप!
जानकारी के मुताबिक, जम्मू-कश्मीर के कठुआ जिले के मढ़ीन तहसील के हांडे चक गांव में सफेद और पीले रंग का हवाई जहाज के आकार का एक गुब्बारा मिला है. गुब्बारे पर PIA लिखा है. यह पाकिस्तान की सरकारी विमानन कंपनी है, जिसका मुख्यालय कराची में स्थित है. जानकारी के अनुसार, गांव के एक बच्चे ने इस गुब्बारे को देखा, जिसके बाद इसकी सूचना पुलिस पोस्ट मढ़ीन को जानकारी दी गई. सूचना मिलने के बाद पुलिस के जवान मौके पर पहुंचे और संदिग्ध गुब्बारे को अपने कब्जे में ले लिया. पुलिस अब इसकी जांच कर रही है.
रिपोर्ट- साहिल केरनी

title: राहुल गांधी को 'सुप्रीम' राहत, ED-CBI नहीं करेगी आय से अधिक संपत्ति के आरोपों की जांच; हाईकोर्ट में फिर होगी सुनवाई
description: राहुल गांधी को सुप्रीम कोर्ट से बड़ी राहत मिली है. SC ने CBI और ED को कांग्रेस नेता के खिलाफ आय से अधिक संपत्ति के आरोपों की जांच करने के हाईकोर्ट के आदेश को खारिज कर दिया है.
author: अभिनव त्रिपाठी
content:
सुप्रीम कोर्ट से कांग्रेस सांसद राहुल गांधी को बड़ी राहत मिली है. शीर्ष न्यायालय ने इलाहाबाद हाईकोर्ट के उस आदेश को खारिज कर दिया है, जिसमें CBI और ED को कांग्रेस नेता के खिलाफ आय से अधिक संपत्ति के आरोपों की जांच करने का निर्देश दिया गया था. मामले की सुनवाई के दौरान सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने राहुल गांधी के खिलाफ आय से अधिक संपत्ति के आरोपों वाली याचिका को नए सिरे से विचार करने के लिए इलाहाबाद हाई कोर्ट के पास वापस भेज दिया है.
दरअसल, सीजेआई जस्टिस सूर्यकांत, जस्टिस जॉयमाल्य बागची और जस्टिस वी मोहना की पीठे ने इस मामले में सुनवाई की और फिर से इस आदेश पर नए सिरे से विचार करने के लिए याचिका को हाईकोर्ट भेज दिया.
इलाहाबाद हाईकोर्ट ने केंद्रीय जांच एजेंसियों को आदेश दिया था कि वे कांग्रेस नेता राहुल गांधी पर लगे आय से अधिक संपत्ति के आरोपों की जांच करें. इस संबंध में हाईकोर्ट ने आदेश भी जारी किया था. इसी आदेश को कांग्रेस नेता ने सुप्रीम कोर्ट में चुनौती दी थी. अब मामले की सुनवाई के बाद सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने इसपर नए सिरे से विचार करने को कहा है.
बता दें कि इस मामले की सुनवाई के दौरान शीर्ष न्यायालय ने याचिका की सुनवाई करते हुए कार्यवाही का ऑडियो बंद कर दिया था. मामले के शिकायतकर्ता विग्नेश शिशिर भी आदालत के सामने पेश हुए थे. उनके व्यक्तिगत रूप से कोर्ट के सामने पेश होने के वजह से सुनवाई की ऑडियो-वीडियो बंद कर दी गई थी.
गौरतलब है कि इससे पहले सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने हाईकोर्ट से कहा था कि वह आय से अधिक संपत्ति के आरोपों से जुड़े मामले में आगे की कार्रवाई को रोक दे. इसके अलावा कोर्ट ने सीबीआई और ED को भी निर्देश दिया था कि वे राहुल गांधी के खिलाफ इस मामले में हाई कोर्ट के आदेशों के तहत कोई रिपोर्ट दाखिल न करें.
हालिया सुनवाई के दौरान हाईकोर्ट ने कहा था कि सीबीआई की ओर से दाखिल हलफनामा उसके पिछले आदेश के अनुरूप नहीं है. इसमें याचिकाकर्ता की ओर से राहुल गांधी की संपत्ति को लेकर की गई शिकायत पर अब तक हुई प्रगति के बारे में कोई स्पष्ट जानकारी नहीं दी गई थी. वहीं, बाद में इलाहाबाद हाईकोर्ट ने नई दिल्ली स्थित CBI के अधिकारी से कहा था कि वे खुद न्यायालय के सामने पेश हों और मामले में हुई जांच की प्रगति के बारे में जानकारी दें.

title: 'Govt Acted Correctly, Prevented Major Disturbance': Dargah Secretary Defends Tamil Nadu's Karthigai Deepam Decision Amid Row
description: Arif Khan, Secretary of the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Dargah, defended the Tamil Nadu government's decision to light the Karthigai Deepam near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple, citing Agama traditions and long-standing practices amid the Thiruparankundram controversy.
author: Asian News International
content:
'Govt Acted Correctly, Prevented Major Disturbance': Dargah Secretary Defends Tamil Nadu's Karthigai Deepam Decision Amid Row
Arif Khan, Secretary of the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Dargah, defended the Tamil Nadu government's decision to light the Karthigai Deepam near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple, citing Agama traditions and long-standing practices amid the Thiruparankundram controversy.
- India News
- 4 min read
Madurai: Amid the ongoing controversy over the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at Thiruparankundram Hill, Arif Khan, Secretary of the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Dargah, on Wednesday defended the Tamil Nadu government's decision, saying the lamp was lit at its usual location in accordance with the temple's Agama traditions and long-standing practices.
Speaking to ANI on the issue, Khan said it was incorrect to claim that the state government had not lit the lamp, and appreciated its handling of the law-and-order situation to prevent religious clashes and communal divisions.
"It is not correct to say that the Tamil Nadu government did not light the lamp. The lamp was lit. In accordance with the temple's Agama traditions and long-standing practices, the government ensured that the lamp was lit at its usual location near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple atop Thiruparankundram Hill. There has been no deviation from the established practice," he said.
Thanking the state government for its handling of the situation, Khan said the authorities had taken a clear stand after considering the legal and religious aspects of the matter.
Advertisement
"I would like to thank the Tamil Nadu government for handling the law-and-order situation effectively and preventing any religious clashes or communal divisions in the state. The government took a clear and decisive stand. The authorities are well aware of the law. If the Tamil Nadu government has taken such a decision, it would certainly have considered all the legal aspects before doing so," he said.
He further said that temple priests had held consultations on the proposed arrangement before arriving at a decision.
Advertisement
"The government also considered the Agama requirements governing the lighting of the lamp. Even yesterday afternoon, the temple priests held consultations to determine whether the proposed arrangement was appropriate. Only after considering all these aspects did they arrive at a decision. They have also issued a statement today," Khan said.
Emphasising that the government had prevented a potentially major disturbance in the state, he said, "The government has acted correctly. Most importantly, it has prevented a potentially major disturbance in Tamil Nadu. That is what we appreciate. The government has discharged its responsibility properly. There is no question of the government violating the law. It has simply followed the established practice that has been observed for generations."
The remarks come amid a political and religious controversy over the non-lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram Hill, despite the Supreme Court's interim order directing that the lamp be lit there.
The Maha Deepam was instead lit near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple as part of the annual Karthigai Deepam festival on Tuesday, while police personnel were deployed near the Deepathoon ahead of the scheduled ceremony.
BJP leader Sudhanshu Trivedi, earlier in the day, accused the Tamil Nadu government and the INDIA bloc of failing to comply with the Supreme Court's order.
Addressing a press conference, Trivedi alleged that the state government had not implemented the court's direction permitting the ceremonial lighting of the lamp at the disputed hilltop pillar for one day, subject to certain conditions.
He also questioned Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the issue, alleging that the INDIA bloc's position contradicted its stated commitment to protecting the Constitution.
Trivedi further criticised the detentions made during the protests and questioned whether the state machinery would take similar action against Muslim clerics during Eid festivities.
Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) International President Alok Kumar also condemned the Tamil Nadu government, alleging that denying permission to light the Maha Deepam at the sacred hill amounted to defiance of the Supreme Court's order and hurt the religious sentiments of devotees.
"The Hindu society will certainly respond democratically, at the appropriate time, to this mindset that hurts the sentiments of devotees and commits contempt of the Judiciary," he said.
Kumar alleged that the state government's decision amounted to challenging the judiciary and the Constitution, and expressed confidence that the Supreme Court would take action against those who had allegedly defied its order.
Meanwhile, Madurai Police, earlier in the day, said cases had been registered against around 300 BJP and Hindu organisation members for staging protests in Thiruparankundram on Tuesday, demanding that the lamp be lit at the Deepathoon.
According to police, cases were registered under six sections, including unlawful assembly without permission, causing a breach of public peace, making controversial remarks and obstructing government servants from discharging their duties.
The protests followed the lighting of the Maha Deepam near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple instead of the Deepathoon, despite the Supreme Court's interim direction.

title: CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy Steps Down After 11 Years; Who Will Lead Flipkart Next?
description: While Flipkart stated that a permanent successor will be announced in the coming weeks, the company confirmed that Chief Product and Technology Officer Balaji Thiagarajan, alongside the company’s board, will lead the organisation on an interim basis.
author: Namya Kapur
content:
CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy Steps Down After 11 Years; Who Will Lead Flipkart Next?
While Flipkart stated that a permanent successor will be announced in the coming weeks, the company confirmed that Chief Product and Technology Officer Balaji Thiagarajan, alongside the company’s board, will lead the organisation on an interim basis.
- India News
- 2 min read
New Delhi: In a major leadership shake-up in India’s e-commerce sector, Walmart-owned Flipkart Group on Wednesday announced that its long-serving Chief Executive Officer, Kalyan Krishnamurthy, will step down from his role, concluding a transformative stint spanning more than 11 years with the company.
While Flipkart stated that a permanent successor will be announced in the coming weeks, the company confirmed that Chief Product and Technology Officer Balaji Thiagarajan, alongside the company’s board, will lead the organisation on an interim basis.
Krishnamurthy’s departure marks the end of an era for the Bengaluru-headquartered giant. He first joined Flipkart in May 2013 as interim head of sales and finance before moving to early investor Tiger Global Management in late 2014.
Returning in June 2016 to head the Category Design Organisation, he was elevated to CEO in January 2017—steering the company through a critical transition as co-founders Sachin and Binny Bansal stepped back from executive control.
Advertisement
Following Walmart’s landmark $16 billion acquisition of a controlling stake in Flipkart in 2018, Krishnamurthy took over as Group CEO.
Under his stewardship, Flipkart’s business grew more than fivefold. He spearheaded the aggressive expansion of its flagship annual Big Billion Days sale, introduced regional-language interfaces and voice assistance to onboard next-wave shoppers, and diversified the platform into grocery, fintech, and quick-commerce via Flipkart Minutes.
Advertisement
"It has been a privilege to be part of Flipkart's journey. I am proud of the scale of the business we have built, but equally proud of how we have built it," Krishnamurthy said in a statement, emphasising that strong ethics and governance remained central to the firm's growth.
Chris Nicholas, President and CEO of Walmart International, praised Krishnamurthy’s leadership, noting that "both Flipkart and Walmart are better because of Kalyan," while reaffirming Walmart’s long-term commitment to the Indian market.
The leadership transition comes at a pivotal moment for Flipkart. Having completed the shift of its holding-company domicile from Singapore to India earlier this year to pave the way for a domestic stock market debut, the company faces heightened competition from quick-commerce rivals and mounting speculation surrounding the timeline of its much-anticipated Initial Public Offering (IPO).

title: 'Biggest Contempt of Constitutional Authority': BJP Targets TVK-Congress Over Karthigai Deepam Row
description: In Ramanathapuram, members of the Hindu Front staged a protest against the state government, accusing it of not implementing the Supreme Court's order. Kenikarai police, who were deployed for security, detained those involved in the road blockade.
author: Namya Kapur
content:
'Biggest Contempt of Constitutional Authority': BJP Targets TVK-Congress Over Karthigai Deepam Row
In Ramanathapuram, members of the Hindu Front staged a protest against the state government, accusing it of not implementing the Supreme Court's order. Kenikarai police, who were deployed for security, detained those involved in the road blockade.
- India News
- 3 min read
New Delhi: BJP leader Sudhanshu Trivedi on Wednesday accused the INDIA bloc and the Tamil Nadu government of not complying with the Supreme Court's order for the one-time ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the disputed hilltop Deepathoon stone pillar on Thirupparankundram Hill in Madurai.
Addressing a press conference, Trivedi said, “Today, I want to draw your attention to what we consider the biggest constitutional contempt committed by the INDI alliance and the Tamil Nadu government. On the occasion of Kartik Purnima yesterday, the Tamil Nadu government did not comply with the Supreme Court's order allowing the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam for just one day, subject to certain conditions. They have neither followed nor implemented the Supreme Court's judgement."
He slammed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for "always displaying" the Constitution book but not following the Supreme Court's order. "I want to ask the INDI alliance, the Congress Party and Rahul Gandhi: you always try to put the Constitution in your pocket, and now you are not ready to uphold the judgement given by the Supreme Court, which is the custodian of the Constitution. I think this is the biggest and dastardly example of contempt against the Constitution by the so-called self-proclaimed Pioneers of the constitutional defence," he said.
Slamming the detentions made on the day, he also asked if the TVK government would commit the same act during Eid festivities by arresting clerics. "Nothing exemplifies my temper more than the episode that involved the arrest of Jain Saraswati Dev Shankaracharya of Kanchi. Would the state machinery dare to arrest a Muslim cleric during Eid festivities? "Who has written this? Former President of India and Bharat Ratna and a very senior leader of the Congress Party, Pranab Mukherjee, in his book... This utter contempt for the court is motivated by the INDI alliance’s malicious design to eradicate Sanatan Dharma—a goal reflected in conferences currently being held in Tamil Nadu—which is orchestrated and linked to an international, nefarious plot to dismantle global Hindutva," he said.
Advertisement
Trivedi further described Karthigai Deepam as an important occasion for Hindu culture and religion and alleged that the controversy was part of an attempt to undermine Sanatan Dharma. “Eradication of Sanatan Dharma is motivated by the evil intention of the INDIA alliance,” he said.
Drawing a parallel with the Shah Bano case, Trivedi said the controversy could become another such episode involving the Congress and its allies. “It will be another Shah Bano event of the Congress alliance,” he said. He also questioned the INDIA bloc's understanding of secularism, alleging that Hindu religious sentiments were being hurt despite political leaders raising the issue only briefly.
Advertisement
Earlier today, multiple organisations held protests at several places in Tamil Nadu over the non-lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon stone pillar in Thiruparankundram, despite the Supreme Court's interim order, with protesters blocking roads and demanding that the state government comply with the court's directions.
In Ramanathapuram, members of the Hindu Front staged a protest against the state government, accusing it of not implementing the Supreme Court's order. Kenikarai police, who were deployed for security, detained those involved in the road blockade. In Pollachi, members of the Hindu Munnani staged a road blockade in the central part of the town on the occasion of the Maha Karthigai Deepam festival. Protesters said Hindu organisations, including Hindu Munnani, the BJP and the Vishva Hindu Parishad, had been continuously protesting since last year over the court orders and the lighting of the Deepam.

title: India opens doors to prized missile test range for Japan for first time, hypersonics collaboration on cards
description: Japan was once a military force constitutionally constrained to an exclusively defensive role. However, it is now gradually becoming a force with long-range strike capabilities, an expanding defence industry and a much greater role in Indo-Pacific security
author: Snehesh Alex Philip
content:
India opens doors to prized missile test range for Japan for first time, hypersonics collaboration on cards
Japan was once a military force constitutionally constrained to an exclusively defensive role. However, it is now gradually becoming a force with long-range strike capabilities, an expanding defence industry and a much greater role in Indo-Pacific security
In a major shift in India's defence cooperation policy, New Delhi is preparing to open up its most prized missile-testing facility to a foreign country for the first time, allowing Japan to use the Defence Research and Development Organisation's (DRDO) Integrated Test Range (ITR) at Chandipur in Odisha for its missile programme.
Not just Chandipur, India is also open to allowing Japan access to two upcoming state-of-the-art testing facilities in West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh, government sources told Firstpost.
The move goes beyond providing testing infrastructure. The two countries are also exploring the possibility of sharing technical know-how and collaborating on advanced missile programmes, including hypersonic weapons, sources said.
They added that India and Japan are also looking at cooperating on the shipbuilding front, especially warships. Sources clarified that, contrary to reports of plans to build Mogani-class multi-mission stealth frigates in India, both sides are working on sharing technical know-how and design features.
India has offered its shipyards and defence PSUs to Japan for collaboration, as well as manufacturing for Tokyo itself and exports from India.
Sources explained that manufacturing in India will be cheaper for Japan, and that this is something under discussion. For example, plans are not just to manufacture the Unicorn (Unified Complex Radio Antenna) for the Indian Navy's requirements but also for exports by Japan itself.
These were among the key issues discussed during the India-Japan 2+2 dialogue last week, led by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar.
Following the meeting, the two countries signed a Letter of Intent (LoI) on the utilisation of firing ranges in India.
Why Japan is keen for Indian firing ranges
Under the arrangement, Japan's Self-Defence Forces will, for the first time, be able to conduct live-fire training in India, including trials involving surface-to-ship missiles such as the Type-25, a next-generation anti-ship missile with a reported range of around 1,000 km.
Both sides will now work towards accelerating coordination between their respective defence authorities to operationalise the arrangement at the earliest. Japan is also in talks with Australia for the test ranges.
Japan is undergoing one of the most significant transformations in its military posture since the Second World War.
What was once a military force constitutionally constrained to an exclusively defensive role is gradually becoming a force with long-range strike capabilities, an expanding defence industry and a much greater role in Indo-Pacific security.
Sources said a Japanese military team had visited India in October to assess various missile-testing facilities. The team spent about a week examining potential ranges where Japan could conduct missile trials as well as test its small attack drones.
Japan faces geographical constraints at home, particularly in identifying sufficiently large and safe maritime corridors for long-range missile firing. India's eastern coastline, with its established missile-testing infrastructure and access to the Bay of Bengal, offers an attractive alternative.
Sources said the discussions are not limited to access to testing facilities. India and Japan are also looking at sharing technical expertise and exploring opportunities for collaboration in advanced weapons programmes, particularly hypersonic technologies.
Japan is seeking to develop a multi-layered coastal defence system incorporating large numbers of relatively inexpensive unmanned aerial, surface and underwater vehicles for reconnaissance and attack missions.
These capabilities would complement its growing arsenal of stand-off missiles, which are designed to strike targets from outside an adversary's engagement range.
Tokyo is developing a new generation of missiles to strengthen deterrence against China's growing military activity around its periphery and respond to North Korea's increasingly sophisticated missile arsenal.
Why the Integrated Test Range matters
The Integrated Test Range at Chandipur is among India's most strategically important defence-testing facilities. It is a critical part of the country's missile-development ecosystem, providing the infrastructure required to launch, track and validate advanced missile systems.
Its capabilities include sophisticated radars, telemetry systems, electro-optical tracking equipment and mission-control infrastructure, which allow DRDO scientists to monitor missile trajectories and assess their performance during flight trials.
The facility has played an important role in testing several Indian missile systems, including air-defence and ballistic missile defence interceptors.
Opening up such infrastructure to Japan would mark a significant expansion of bilateral defence cooperation, taking the relationship beyond joint military exercises and conventional defence technology partnerships, sources said.

title: Dalai Lama gets Lutyens' Delhi bungalow as India gives his office a permanent base in capital
description: The Dalai Lama will continue to be based in Dharamshala, but his office now has a dedicated facility in Lutyens' Delhi for official engagements
author: FP News Desk
content:
Dalai Lama gets Lutyens' Delhi bungalow as India gives his office a permanent base in capital
The Dalai Lama will continue to be based in Dharamshala, but his office now has a dedicated facility in Lutyens' Delhi for official engagements
The Indian government has allotted a bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi to the office of the 14th Dalai Lama, giving the Tibetan spiritual leader a dedicated base in the national capital for his visits and official engagements.
The property, located at 20 Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane, has been allotted to the Gaden Phodrang Trust, which serves as the Dalai Lama's official office and manages his spiritual and humanitarian work.
The allotment followed a request from the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), as per news agency PTI. While the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry has not issued an official statement, government accommodation of this kind is generally allotted for three years, with the possibility of an extension.
Security upgrades worth nearly Rs 35 lakh are being carried out at the property. These include reinforced gates, a security cabin and additional protective structures along the boundary wall. The work is intended to strengthen security and regulate access to the premises.
Why does the Dalai Lama need a base in Delhi?
The Dalai Lama's primary residence is in McLeod Ganj, near Dharamshala in Himachal Pradesh, where he has lived since fleeing Tibet in 1959.
He escaped Tibet amid a Chinese crackdown and unrest in Lhasa, eventually reaching India on March 31, 1959. New Delhi granted him asylum, beginning a relationship that has continued for more than six decades. India has since been home to the Dalai Lama and a large Tibetan refugee community.
Although he is based in Dharamshala, the Dalai Lama travels to the national capital for meetings, engagements and other official work. Having a dedicated facility in Delhi is expected to reduce the logistical challenges involved in arranging accommodation and security for him and his staff.
The new bungalow will also provide his office with a permanent base from which to coordinate engagements and its work on Tibetan culture, humanitarian causes and interfaith dialogue.
What is the Gaden Phodrang Trust?
The bungalow has been allotted to the Gaden Phodrang Trust rather than to the Dalai Lama as a private residence.
Gaden Phodrang is the official office of the Dalai Lama. It was registered as a private trust in India in 2011, after he voluntarily gave up his political authority in favour of an elected Tibetan leadership.
The trust is dedicated to preserving the institution of the Dalai Lama and supporting his spiritual and humanitarian work. Its stated commitments include promoting human values, encouraging interfaith harmony, preserving Tibetan culture and identity, protecting the environment and promoting a deeper understanding of ancient Indian wisdom.
The distinction is important: the new facility is intended to support the institution and office of the Dalai Lama, not to shift his residence from Dharamshala to Delhi.
Tibetan leadership welcomes India's move
The allotment has been welcomed by the Tibetan leadership in exile.
Dolma Tsering, Speaker of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, expressed gratitude to the Indian government, saying the accommodation would make the Dalai Lama's visits to the capital more convenient and provide greater comfort and security during his stays.
'This is very welcome news. The accommodation will make His Holiness the Dalai Lama's visits to the national capital far more convenient and provide greater comfort and security during his stays in New Delhi,' she said as cited by news agency ANI.
Choedak Gyatso, a member of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile's standing committee, also welcomed the decision, describing it as a reaffirmation of India's longstanding support for the Tibetan people.
The next Dalai Lama and the battle over who gets to choose
The allotment also comes amid growing international attention on the Dalai Lama's succession, with a US congressional panel recently urging Washington to coordinate with New Delhi on the process.
The bipartisan US-China Economic and Security Review Commission has recommended that the US recognise the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole authority to identify his successor and reject any candidate selected or appointed by Beijing.
It has also called for intelligence-sharing and contingency planning with India, warning that China could use political pressure, cyber operations and disinformation to influence the succession.

title: Delhi reports 83 new lung cancer patients a month, 1 death every 3 days: Air pollution to blame?
description: Around 83 cases of lung cancer were recorded every month across prominent government hospitals in the national capital in the last six and a half year period, with one patient succumbing to the disease every three days
author: Tanishq.Priya
content:
Delhi reports 83 new lung cancer patients a month, 1 death every 3 days: Air pollution to blame?
Around 83 cases of lung cancer were recorded every month across prominent government hospitals in the national capital in the last six and a half year period, with one patient succumbing to the disease every three days
Around 83 cases of lung cancer were recorded every month across prominent government hospitals in the national capital in the last six and a half year period, with one patient succumbing to the disease every three days.
This information was provided in response to an RTI query to AIIMS, RML Hospital, Safdarjung Hospital and the Delhi State Cancer Institute.
Under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, data regarding lung cancer cases and associated deaths between January 1, 2020, and July 31, 2026, were requested from the hospitals. Safdarjung Hospital only provided the number of lung cancer deaths but did not disclose the total number of cases.
A request was also made for data on patients who had never smoked. However, none of the institutes provided any data on it.
According to information provided in response to separate RTI applications filed by PTI Bhasha, 6,581 lung cancer cases were recorded across three of the four hospitals (excluding Safdarjung), averaging 83 cases per month. Across all four hospitals, 913 deaths were reported, which translates to one patient dying every three days.
The national capital is currently grappling with a severe air pollution crisis, an annual affair now in November, which is observed as the Lung Cancer Awareness Month.
Although health experts state that long-term exposure to air pollution increases the risk of lung cancer, it is not the sole cause. Smoking and genetic mutations are two of the other contributing factors.
The highest number of cases was recorded at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). This central government hospital provided data for the period from January 2020 to March 2026, during which 4,860 cases of lung cancer were registered and 158 deaths occurred. This averages to approximately 65 cases per month, with two patient deaths occurring monthly.
According to data from the Delhi State Cancer Institute (DSCI), 1,613 cases of lung cancer were reported between January 1, 2020, and July 2026, resulting in 354 deaths. This translates to an average of 20 cases per month, with four patient deaths occurring monthly during this period.
The institute noted that in 2021, the disease was also diagnosed in two children, and over a span of about six and a half years, 351 women were found to be suffering from lung cancer. However, it did not provide a gender-segregated breakdown of the deaths.
Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital reported 108 cases of lung cancer during this period, including 47 women, with eight deaths recorded. Safdarjung Hospital reported 393 deaths among patients suffering from lung cancer during the same timeframe.
A senior doctor at the DSCI, speaking to PTI on the condition of anonymity, mentioned that the institute receives patients not only from Delhi but also from Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Bihar, and even Nepal.
Regarding the role of air pollution in Delhi on lung cancer cases, the doctor said the primary cause is smoking or exposure to tobacco smoke, though genetic mutations also play a role.
According to doctors, lung cancer has also been detected in non-smoking women; this is suspected to be linked to genetic mutations and pollution.
Doctors also said that the disease is often diagnosed only in its final stages, making treatment extremely challenging.
Dr Geeta Kadayaprath, a senior specialist at the Apollo Athenaa Women’s Cancer Centre, said that long-term exposure to polluted air—common in cities like Delhi—can increase the risk of lung cancer.
She noted that the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), under the World Health Organization, has classified outdoor air pollution and the particulate matter it contains as carcinogenic to humans.
She explained that PM 2.5 particles are so minute that they can penetrate deep into the lungs and, over time, cause damage to cells.
When asked about symptoms, Dr Vikas Maurya, a senior specialist at Fortis Hospital in Shalimar Bagh, explained that there are often no clear symptoms in the early stages.
However, potential warning signs include a persistent cough, coughing up blood, shortness of breath, chest pain, changes in one’s voice, unexplained weight loss, and recurring chest infections.
He further noted that the condition cannot be detected through a standard X-ray; instead, a CT scan is required for diagnosis.
(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by Firstpost staff.)

title: 1 year on, firms struggle to fully implement 4 labour codes, finds survey
description: A new survey finds that payroll and compliance changes are the biggest implementation challenges, cited by 73.5 per cent of respondents, while 74.4 per cent expect employment costs to rise
author: Barkha Mathur
content:
1 year on, firms struggle to fully implement 4 labour codes, finds survey
A new survey finds that payroll and compliance changes are the biggest implementation challenges, cited by 73.5 per cent of respondents, while 74.4 per cent expect employment costs to rise
Listen to This Article
Just over half of organisations surveyed consider themselves fully prepared to implement India's four labour codes, a year after they came into effect, even as companies continue to grapple with payroll and compliance changes, interpretation of the revised wage definition and pending state-level rules, according to a Grant Thornton Bharat report.
The report, Labour codes: Implementation pulse, released on Wednesday, draws on responses from more than 200 organisations across sectors, including technology, manufacturing, financial services, professional services, education, energy, infrastructure and hospitality.
The survey found that 50.6 per cent of respondents described themselves as fully prepared, while 28.8 per cent were still preparing for implementation. Another 11.7 per cent had not started the process and 9 per cent were not aware of the changes.
However, overall preparedness has not necessarily translated into changes in workplace policies and processes. While 54.3 per cent of respondents had completed an impact assessment of the codes, only 41.9 per cent had reviewed their human resources (HR) policies and employment contracts for gaps.
The four labour codes, which consolidate 29 central labour laws covering wages, social security, industrial relations and occupational safety, came into effect on November 21, 2025.
Also Read
Revised wage definition likely to push up employment costs
About 66.2 per cent of respondents said they had reviewed and updated their salary structures in line with the revised definition, while another 10.5 per cent planned to undertake the exercise. However, 74.4 per cent expected the change to increase employment costs.
The report said that nearly half of respondents, or 49.6 per cent, estimated that employment costs would increase by up to 5 per cent, while 12 per cent expected an increase of more than 5 per cent. Another 12.8 per cent said they did not expect any impact, while an equal proportion could not estimate the effect.
Gratuity was identified as the component most likely to see an increase, with 43.6 per cent of respondents flagging it, followed by provident fund contributions at 30.8 per cent.
The additional cost will require companies to decide how much of the increase they are willing to absorb. While 49.6 per cent of respondents said they planned to absorb it, 29.9 per cent were still evaluating their approach, while 20.5 per cent did not plan to absorb the increase.
Payroll and compliance changes remain biggest hurdles
Although 48.7 per cent of organisations said their payroll software was fully ready, another 31.6 per cent were still upgrading their systems. A further 13.7 per cent said their systems were not ready, while 6 per cent reported technical difficulties linked to the deemed wage provisions.
According to the report, payroll and compliance changes were the leading implementation challenge that 73.5 per cent of respondents flagged, followed by HR policy revisions at 66.7 per cent and legal interpretation of the revised wage definition at 55.6 per cent. Employee communication and technology were cited by 36.8 per cent and 35.9 per cent, respectively.
The requirement to complete full and final settlement of wages within two working days also remains an area of unfinished work. Only 38.8 per cent of respondents said they had implemented the requirement, while 33.1 per cent were discussing its implementation. Another 23.8 per cent considered it impractical, and 4.4 per cent were unaware of the change.
Pending state-level rules are another constraint on implementation. As many as 77.8 per cent of respondents indicated that finalisation of state rules was important for complete readiness. Among them, 43.6 per cent said the absence of final rules had a moderate impact on their readiness, while 34.2 per cent reported a significant impact.
The areas where companies sought further regulatory clarification included the definition of wages and its computation methodology, cited by 24.8 per cent of respondents. Deployment of contractual workers in core activities was flagged by 23.1 per cent, while 19.7 per cent sought clarity on the two-working-day full and final settlement requirement.
Workforce deployment through contractors is also likely to be affected. About 65.8 per cent of respondents expected the labour codes to influence how they deploy contractual workers. The report recommends that companies review workforce classifications, contractor arrangements and agreements with manpower providers, particularly where workers are engaged in activities considered core to an establishment.
Despite these implementation gaps, about 72 per cent of respondents said they were either somewhat or very confident about implementing the codes.

title: No global power wants India to progress, says RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat

content:
No global power wants India to progress, says RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
He was speaking at the inauguration of the fifth Padmaa Festival in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
Listen to This Article
Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Wednesday said that no power in the world wants India to progress, as global powers seek to assert their dominance and keep others under pressure, believing in the principle of the 'survival of the fittest'.
He was speaking at the inauguration of the fifth Padmaa Festival in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.
Local organisation Gyanyajnah Foundation has organised the three-day Padmaa Festival, which brings together Padma awardees from diverse fields to interact with people.
Bhagwat said that India wants to help everyone and extends assistance even to nations that hate it.
"No power in the world wants India to progress because they only seek power and believe in the principle of the 'survival of the fittest', keeping everyone under pressure. If India grows, their shops will be shut because India wants to help everyone. India helps even its neighbours who hate it," he said.
Also Read
The RSS chief said the younger generation was free from the influences of slavery.
"If someone speaks genuinely, the youth are prepared to stand behind him. They hate lies and want to make their country great," he said.
Former Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General Anil Chauhan (Retd), who also shared the stage with Bhagwat at the event, said the youth will be the biggest contributors to and beneficiaries of 'Viksit Bharat'.
The inauguration ceremony took place at the Manthan Hall of MIT Campus located on Beed Bypass Road in the city. Interactive sessions involving the Padma Shri awardees will take place at the Manthan Hall from Wednesday afternoon, the organisers have said.

title: Meta delegation meets Congress as protests intensify over content curbs

author: Reuters
content:
Meta delegation meets Congress as protests intensify over content curbs
Meta's Aman Jain and Natasha Jog, two key executives in India, represented the company at the meeting at Congress headquarters on Tuesday
Listen to This Article
Meta's top executives in India held closed-door talks with the country's opposition Congress party as the two sides try to ‌defuse escalating tensions amid protests against the US firm's content moderation practices, four people familiar with the matter said.
Meta's Aman Jain and Natasha Jog, two key executives in India, represented the company at the meeting at Congress headquarters on Tuesday, one person said.
They raised concerns about protests targeting Meta's offices and the depiction ‌of CEO Mark Zuckerberg in posters. Congress raised concerns about a rise in restrictions on its leaders' accounts and posts, and about allegations that Meta favours the ruling party, three other people said. Meta has denied any favoritism.
The meeting marked Meta's first direct engagement with the party since protests by its youth ‌wing began on Friday.
The Youth Congress has demanded that Meta restore accounts taken down on ‌government orders and explain how its algorithms restrict posts, ‌and its workers have clashed with police near Meta's offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram.
Congress did ‌not immediately respond to a request for comment, while Meta said it moderates content in India in accordance with ‌the law.

title: Mint Explainer | Why the government is launching the fifth edition of Nayi Chetna
description: Nayi Chetna 5.0 seeks to move towards measurable improvements in women's access to livelihoods, financial resources, assets, safe mobility and decision-making.
author: Vijay C Roy
content:
The fifth edition of the government’s national gender campaign, Nayi Chetna – Pahal Badlav Ki, will be implemented nationwide from 25 November to 23 December under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission. The campaign is aimed at promoting equality and empowering India’s female population, which, according to World Bank 2024 data, stood at 702.6 million, or 48.4% of the total.
Mint explains the rationale behind the new edition of the campaign.
Why is the government launching the fifth edition of Nayi Chetna?
Nayi Chetna has evolved since it started in 2022 into a nationwide campaign to address gender-based violence, challenge discriminatory social norms and promote gender equality. While previous editions focused on awareness and collective action, Nayi Chetna 5.0 seeks to move towards measurable improvements in women's access to livelihoods, financial resources, assets, safe mobility and decision-making.
The campaign seeks to address structural barriers that restrict women's participation in economic activities and their ability to exercise control over household and financial decisions. The theme of Nayi Chetna 5.0 is: “From Access to Agency: Empowering Women through Livelihoods and Equal Opportunities for a Viksit Bharat.”
"When women are free to dream and earn, they change their own lives and the lives around them," said Aditi B Singla, founder of Pure Karma Foundation, an NGO.
What is the significance of the theme?
The theme is about providing women access to opportunities and enabling them to exercise control over their choices and resources. Access to bank accounts, credit, government welfare schemes, employment opportunities and livelihood programmes is an important first step.
However, economic empowerment also requires women to have control over their earnings, assets and financial decisions. Having a bank account does not necessarily mean a woman independently controls the money deposited in it. Participation in a self-help group or livelihood programme may not automatically translate into greater decision-making power within the household.
The government seeks to strengthen women's ability to make independent economic choices, participate in markets and access opportunities without facing social or institutional restrictions. The broader objective is to ensure that women are recognized not merely as beneficiaries of government programmes but as economic contributors and decision makers.
Which four interconnected focus areas has the government identified?
The fifth edition will place women’s economic empowerment at the centre of its approach, with a focus on four interconnected areas: recognizing women as economic contributors, strengthening their access to and control over assets, promoting safe mobility, and redistributing unpaid care work.
The campaign aims to move beyond awareness generation towards coordinated action and measurable improvements in women’s economic participation, agency and decision-making.
What role will self-help groups and gender resource centres play in implementing the campaign?
Self-help groups, village organizations, cluster-level federations and other community institutions under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission will play a central role in implementing the campaign. They provide established grassroots networks through which women can participate in collective activities, access livelihood opportunities and raise concerns affecting their communities.
Gender resource centres will be strengthened as community-level platforms to help women access government services, welfare entitlements, legal assistance, support systems and grievance redressal mechanisms.
“It is important to create awareness among women about their rights and opportunities, with the support of local stakeholders, leaders and NGOs. Equally important is connecting them with the right job opportunities so they can become financially independent and empowered,” said Rita Kalra, district governor, Rotary district 3080 comprising five northern states and a Union Territory.
Which ministries and departments are being brought together under the campaign?
Gender inequality involves a range of interconnected issues and addressing them requires coordination across government departments rather than isolated interventions. A framework will be provided for 15 ministries and departments to align their schemes, programmes, institutional mechanisms and frontline networks with the campaign’s objectives.
It will seek to strengthen coordinated interventions at the national, state, district and community levels. The approach is intended to reduce gaps in service delivery and improve women's access to different government interventions through coordinated action.

title: How Tanjot Singh aims to make Delhi's air cleaner: Meet the mind behind India's first bio-based air filtration platform
description: Tanjot Singh is currently a Class 11 student at Delhi Public School, RK Puram. He completed Grade 9 (2025) and 10 (2025) at Lilawati Vidya Mandir
author: Livemint
content:
Tanjot Singh, a student of Delhi Public School (DPS), RK Puram, developed an alternative to conventional HEPA (high efficiency particulate filtration) air-purification filter media using compressed wool felt and electrostatic cotton.
His project has earned him a place among the top 60 national winners at the 12th National Level Exhibition and Project Competition (NLEPC) under the INSPIRE-MANAK programme, an initiative of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, implemented in collaboration with the National Innovation Foundation (NIF)-India.
Here's all you need to know about Tanjot Singh and his award-winning innovation.
Singh is a founder of PraaNavya, an initiative focused on developing climate hardware and deep-tech engineering solutions for cleaner air. According to his blog, PraaNavya is backed by Emergent Ventures US , Antler India and Masters' Union. He had previously co-founded SES Clean Air, his blog stated.
He is currently a Class 11 student at Delhi Public School, RK Puram. He completed Grade 9 (2025) and 10 (2025) at Lilawati Vidya Mandir.
Singh dropped out of school after Grade 10 in 2025-2026 to work full-time on his hardware startup PraaNavya. He self-studied Grade 11–12 Physics and Mathematics, wrote in his blog, built three prototype generations, filed a patent, raised grants, pitched to 30+ stakeholders and deployed school pilots. He rejoined school as an 11th grader in 2026.
According to his blog, Tanjot Singh built his "first serious engineering project" — a 10-foot industrial scrubber — at age 14 with a team of five under CEEW mentorship. That project became the second-largest engineering build in his school's history and laid the foundation for everything that followed, he claimed.
"Today, I'm building PraaNavya — India's first bio-based air filtration platform — with a published patent, school pilots protecting 300+ students, and a clear mission: to build globally scalable climate technologies through engineering research and entrepreneurship," he wrote.
Singh positioned his PraaNavya Climate Tech as "India's first bio-based air filtration platform — sustainable alternatives to disposable HEPA filters." His innovation explores the possibility of using bio-based materials for air filtration while addressing concerns about the disposal of synthetic filter materials.
The problem he aims to solve is Delhi's air pollution crisis. His blog says current solutions (Dyson, Philips, etc.) are expensive, generate massive plastic waste, and are inaccessible to many people. HEPA filters are single-use, petroleum-based, and environmentally costly.
Notably, Conventional air purifiers commonly use HEPA filters, ideal for capturing airborne particles as air passes through a dense network of filter fibres. Although these filters play an important role in improving air quality, their synthetic fibre filters eventually need replacement.
Developed through his initiative, PraaNavya, the prototype uses compressed wool felt and electrostatic cotton as bio-based alternatives to conventional synthetic HEPA filter media, the Times of India reported.
Singh claims that a five-stage bio-based filtration stack — triboelectric wool, electrostatic cotton, activated charcoal, polyester, PLA bio-polymer — achieves 99.7 percent PM2.5/PM10 reduction with ~80 percent less plastic waste than conventional HEPA filters.
Some of the key features he highlighted in his blog are:
> 5-stage filtration — multi-layer bio-based media
> ₹5,000 purifier — with ₹800 biodegradable replacement filters
> 5 application domains — consumer, HVAC, industrial, automotive, respiratory
> Flutter BLE companion app — with AI-powered purifier placement
> Published Indian patent — co-inventor, 2025
Real-world deployment
His innovation, he claims, is currently piloting across two schools, five classrooms — serving 300+ students. An analysis measured ~40 percent lower PM levels in-situ, he wrote, adding that school pilots demonstrate tangible impact: cleaner air, healthier students, validated technology.
The project is backed by Antler India, Masters' Union, ThinkStartup. At Shark Tank India S5 Stage 2, he was selected from 120,000+ startup registrations for virtual pitch submission. Other notable recognitions include: Masters' Union Elevator Pitch — youngest finalist & winner; Youth Ideathon — National Winner (2022) & Top 3 (2025); INSEF National Science Fair — Bronze Medal; InnoHEALTH Young Innovator Awards; EMERGE Sustainable Leaders — National Top 10. He has pitched to 30+ stakeholders including VC firms, IITD, Ministry of Environment, Government of Delhi.

title: Vantara signs 10-year wildlife conservation pact with Madagascar to repatriate trafficked animals — All we know
description: Under the agreement, Vantara will assist in the safe return of Malagasy animals seized overseas and support their rescue, rehabilitation, and veterinary care.
author: Livemint
content:
Vantara has signed a 10-year agreement with Madagascar to help bring animals seized abroad back to their home country, support their rehabilitation, and, where possible, return them to the wild.
The Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre Society (Vantara), based in Jamnagar, Gujarat, and Madagascar’s Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (MEDD) signed the non-exclusive Memorandum of Understanding on wildlife conservation and animal welfare on November 24.
The deal fulfils a commitment Vantara made to India’s CITES Management Authority on August 19. Under the agreement, Vantara will assist in the safe return of Malagasy animals seized overseas and support their rescue, rehabilitation, and veterinary care.
Beyond repatriation, the partnership focuses on building Madagascar’s domestic conservation capacity. Vantara will help train local wildlife experts and may support the construction and establishment of a National Wildlife Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre.
Planned as a national hub for conservation, research, and training, the centre will remain the property of the Republic of Madagascar and operate under MEDD’s authority on government-provided land.
Madagascar is home to species found nowhere else on Earth, many of which are under severe threat. According to the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, 90% of lemur species in the country are threatened with extinction, and nearly a third are Critically Endangered.
The country’s radiated tortoises face a similar crisis. The Turtle Survival Alliance estimates their wild population dropped by more than 47% between the late 1990s and 2013. Madagascar also lost roughly 29% of its tree cover between 2001 and 2023.
Illegal wildlife trade compounds the problem, with Madagascar’s environment minister describing it as the second leading cause of biodiversity decline after habitat loss. Between January and April 2026 alone, rescuers in the country received more than 1,000 tortoises from six confiscation cases.
Bringing seized animals home is often a slow and complicated process. When Thai authorities intercepted 48 lemurs and more than 1,000 tortoises in 2024, 131 tortoises had already died in transit, and others did not survive the weeks that followed.
While Thailand cared for the surviving animals and backed their return, there was no dedicated funding, and complex international permit procedures delayed flights back to Madagascar twice.
Under the new pact, Vantara’s teams can assist at Madagascar’s request across different stages of an animal’s return, including health checks, disease screening, transport, quarantine, and post-arrival care.
Vantara will also share scientific expertise, such as field research and genetic profiling, to help Madagascar decide which animals can be released into the wild and where, in line with IUCN guidelines.
Every final decision will rest solely with the Government of Madagascar, advised by the country's CITES Scientific Authority.
Through training, internships, specialist exchanges, and applied research, the partnership aims to ensure local teams can sustain conservation work long after rescued animals return.
“Madagascar is a biodiversity hotspot of global importance, and our wildlife is part of who we are as a nation. These animals belong to the forests that shaped them,” said H.E. Nolave Luck Aristide Andriatsihala, Minister of Environment and Sustainable Development, Republic of Madagascar.
“Protecting them takes cooperation across borders, and we are grateful to the countries and organisations, such as Vantara, who work with us to safeguard Madagascar's natural heritage,” Andriatsihala added.
MEDD’s Director General of Environmental Governance Rakotondravoninala Valison Kiady said the partnership will focus on practical execution. “Vantara brings world-class expertise in animal rescue, veterinary care and welfare, and we look forward to working together to turn this commitment into concrete actions, from immediate deliverables to long-term, results-oriented programmes, all guided by science, regulations and international best practice,” Kiady said.
Vantara Chief Executive Officer Vivaan Karani said the initiative reflects the organisation's focus on in situ conservation, or protecting animals in their natural home range.
“Madagascar is home to some of the world’s most extraordinary and unique wildlife, and protecting these species in their natural habitats is central to our ten-year conservation strategy,” Karani said. “Our priority is to strengthen the people and institutions working to conserve wildlife in its country of origin. We thank the Government of Madagascar for this partnership and look forward to supporting its long-term conservation priorities, with every decision resting firmly with Madagascar.”

title: 'Ramayana' among top 20 contenders for Oscars visual effects award
description: Nitesh Tiwari's film  Ramayana: Rise of a Legend  has advanced to the top 20 for the 99th Academy Awards. The film features actors such as Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Sai Pallavi as Sita. This year, significant Hollywood films like  Dune: Part Three  and  Avengers: Doomsday  are also in the running. Voting for the Oscar shortlists will begin on December 7 and end on December 11.
author: PTI
content:
Mumbai: Nitesh Tiwari's "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend" has advanced to the top 20 contenders in the visual effects category for the 99th Academy Awards, joining major Hollywood productions such as "Dune: Part Three", "The Odyssey" and "Avengers: Doomsday".
The mythological epic, starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, is among the three projects from Sony Pictures to feature in the list.
Also Read: Oscars 2027: Marathi film 'Gondhal,' Nagaland drama 'Angh' among 104 films in International Feature film race
Multiple sources told Variety that the Visual Effects Branch of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS) has notified the artisans behind the 20 films advancing to the next round ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.
The organisation, however, is yet to officially announce or confirm the list.
Also Read: Lionsgate Play announces AI-led original series ‘Eklavya’, introduces AI actor Yug R.Ai
The top 20 contenders also include Denis Villeneuve's "Dune: Part Three", Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey", Phil Lord and Christopher Miller's "Project Hail Mary", Steven Spielberg's "Disclosure Day" and Marvel Studios' "Avengers: Doomsday", directed by Anthony and Joe Russo.
Disney leads the confirmed titles with four entries -- "Avengers: Doomsday", Jon Favreau's "Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu", "Whalefall" and Thomas Kail's live-action "Moana", featuring Dwayne Johnson reprising his role as Maui.
Skydance has three contenders -- "Dune: Part Three", Alejandro G Inarritu's Tom Cruise-starrer "Digger" and Craig Gillespie's "Supergirl".
Universal Pictures has secured spots for "The Odyssey" and "Disclosure Day", while Amazon MGM Studios has advanced with "Project Hail Mary" and Kyle Balda's "The Sheep Detectives".
Other films in the race include Takashi Yamazaki's "Godzilla Minus Zero", Laika's stop-motion feature "Wildwood", A24's "Backrooms", Paramount's "Heart of the Beast", Netflix's "The Mosquito Bowl" and Lionsgate's "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping".
"Ramayana", which has earned over Rs 1,500 crore at the worldwide box office since its debut in theatres earlier this month, is produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations.
DNEG, the London-based visual effects studio, has won eight Oscars for its work on "Inception" (2011), "Interstellar" (2015), "Ex Machina" (2016), "Blade Runner 2049" (2018), "First Man" (2019), "Tenet" (2021), "Dune" (2022) and "Dune: Part Two" (2025).
Besides "Ramayana", the company has worked on several other Oscar contenders, including "The Odyssey", "Moana", "Supergirl" and "Spider-Man: Brand New Day", according to its official website.
In 2023, SS Rajamouli's "RRR" had also featured among the top 20 contenders in the visual effects category for the 95th Academy Awards but did not make it to the final nominations.
The period action drama, starring Ram Charan and Jr NTR, went on to win the Oscar for Best Original Song for "Naatu Naatu", making it the first Indian song to win the award.
Voting for the Oscar shortlists will begin on December 7 and end on December 11, with the shortlists across categories scheduled to be announced on December 15.
The final nominations will be announced on January 21.
The 99th Academy Awards will be held on March 14 at the Dolby Theatre at Ovation Hollywood and will air live on ABC.

title: Over 74% organizations expect increase in wage cost under the Labour Codes: Grant Thornton Bharat’s Survey
description: After the implementation of Labour Codes, over three-quarters of organizations expect increased employment costs. Organizations are assessing how to manage these costs, with many planning to absorb them. The survey indicates that most organizations are reviewing their compensation policies to align with updated wage definitions. Regulatory clarity is viewed as critical for complete readiness and consistent implementation across the workforce.
author: Yogima Seth Sharma
content:
“Organisations are also taking a considered approach to the incremental cost, with 49.6% planning to absorb it and 29.9% evaluating the most appropriate course,” the Grant Thornton Bharat’s Labour codes: Implementation pulse survey shows.
The survey points to growing preparedness, with 50.6% of respondents describing themselves as fully prepared and 54.3% having completed an impact assessment.
Organisations are proactively responding to the revised wage definition.
Two-thirds of respondents (66.2%) have already reviewed and updated their compensation policies in line with the revised wage definition, while a further 10.5% plan to undertake the exercise, it said.
As per the Survey, done after a year of roll-out of the Code, implementation of labour codes is gathering momentum, with organisations making tangible progress on impact assessments, compensation reviews and payroll preparedness. The focus is now shifting towards embedding the changes consistently across policies, systems and workforce practices, it said.
Over 200 respondents representing organisations ranging from fewer than 100 employees to those with more than 10,000 employees across technology, manufacturing, financial services, professional services, education, energy, infrastructure and hospitality participated and shared insights across various areas were polled under the Survey.
The Survey showed that 77.8% of the respondents said final state rules are important for complete readiness, underscoring how further regulatory clarity can enable location-specific policy, process and system changes.
“Continued regulatory guidance and finalisation of state rules can further accelerate consistent implementation across policies, payroll and workforce practices,” Akhil Chandna, partner and global people solutions leader, Grant Thornton Bharat said.
According to the Survey, payroll and compliance changes remain the most frequently cited implementation priority (73.5%), followed by HR policy revisions (66.7%) and legal interpretation of the wage definition (55.6%).

title: Deepam row: Tamil Nadu files status report in SC, apologises for non-lighting of lamp at Deepathoon
description: The Tamil Nadu government expressed its regret to the Supreme Court regarding the failure to light the ceremonial lamp. The Board of Trustees did not authorize the proposed team for the lighting at Deepathoon. Despite completing all arrangements, the customary practice was followed instead. The district administration made efforts to secure necessary authorisation for the event.
author: PTI
content:
New Delhi, The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday apologised to the Supreme Court over the non-lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the disputed Deepathoon on Thirupparankundram hill on November 24, claiming the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise a team proposed for carrying out the exercise.
In a status report filed by Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna before a bench comprising Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi, the state government said the district administration had completed all arrangements for implementing the apex court's November 20 order permitting the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon through a restricted team authorised by the temple administration.
However, the order of the apex court could not be complied with because the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise the team proposed for carrying out the exercise and instead resolved to follow the customary practice of lighting the Karthigai Mahadeepam at its traditional location, the state government claimed in the report.
"I submit that I took all the steps to comply with the order in good faith. There has been no wilful deliberate disobedience on my part of any directions of this Hon'ble Court. I hold the orders of the Hon'ble Court in the highest respect and remain committed to comply with every direction this Hon'ble Court may issue.
"I sincerely apologise for the lamp not being lit at the Deepathoon. The district administration made every effort to secure the authorisation of the Devasthanam and the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon. However, the Board of Trustees, by its resolution dated November 24, resolved to light the lamp at the customary place. I submit that I will submit an additional status report with all supporting documents along with the same," the status report said.
The District Collector said the administration made every effort to secure authorisation of Devasthanam for lighting of lamp at Deepathoon.
The top court fixed the main plea against the Madras High Court order permitting lighting of ceremonial lamp for final hearing in January next year.
The bench may take up the contempt plea, if any, filed in the matter.
