title: Miss Universe 2026: India's Kaziah Liz Mejo misses Top 12, bows out in Puerto Rico
description: Nineteen-year-old Kaziah Liz Mejo, India's first Miss Universe Keralam, reached the Top 30 at the seventy-fifth Miss Universe pageant in Puerto Rico but missed advancing to the Top 12.
author: Onmanorama Staff
content:
Miss Universe 2026: India's Kaziah Liz Mejo misses Top 12, bows out in Puerto Rico
Mail This Article
India’s Kaziah Liz Mejo, who made it to the Top 30 of the 75th edition of the Miss Universe pageant, failed to advance to the Top 12, missing out on the crown at the international competition held in San Juan, Puerto Rico.
The 19-year-old from Mavelikkara in Keralam’s Alappuzha district represented India at the pageant. She made history earlier this year by becoming the first woman from Keralam to win the Miss Universe India title.
Mejo’s pageant journey gathered momentum in 2026 when she won the Miss Universe Kerala title, becoming the youngest winner of the state competition. On August 23, she was crowned Miss Universe India 2026 in Jaipur, emerging winner from a field of 53 contestants.
The 75th edition of Miss Universe brought together 116 contestants. The finale was held at the José Miguel Agrelot Coliseum in San Juan, with reigning Miss Universe Fátima Bosch of Mexico set to crown her successor.
The anniversary edition also featured a specially designed crown created by George Wittels in collaboration with Paris-based jewellery house Maison d’OR. Made in the Philippines, the crown features 3,150 diamonds set in white gold.
The competition included several rounds, including the national costume presentation, preliminary round and final evening, with contestants assessed on their stage presence and performances.
The 2026 edition also faced controversy over contestant withdrawals, disputes concerning franchise rights and concerns about event management.
India has won the Miss Universe crown three times. Sushmita Sen won the title in 1994, followed by Lara Dutta in 2000 and Harnaaz Sandhu in 2021.

title: BJP, SAD revive alliance ahead of Punjab Assembly polls
description: The BJP and SAD revived their alliance for the upcoming Punjab Assembly elections, promising to contest all one hundred seventeen seats together in what they termed a 'national and emotional' bond.
author: Onmanorama Staff
content:
BJP, SAD revive alliance ahead of Punjab Assembly polls
Mail This Article
New Delhi: The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday announced the revival of their alliance for the upcoming Punjab Assembly elections, describing the partnership as a "national and emotional" bond.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah said the two parties would contest all 117 Assembly seats together, with the SAD getting the chief minister's post.
With the SAD rejoining the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), the coalition was now complete, Shah said, recalling that the relationship between the two parties dated back to the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-L K Advani era.
BJP president Nitin Nabin announced the alliance at a press conference in New Delhi alongside Shah and SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal. He said the two parties would work together to make Punjab a developed state.
Badal described the partnership as an emotional rather than a political alliance.
Shah said the two parties would soon finalise a detailed election manifesto. Key priorities would include eliminating the drug menace in Punjab, working for farmers' welfare and promoting Hindu-Sikh unity, he said.
The Punjab Assembly elections are expected to be held early next year.
The SAD ended its 24-year alliance with the BJP in September 2020 over the three farm laws, which were subsequently repealed. The party had also withdrawn its representative, Harsimrat Kaur Badal, from the Union Cabinet.
In the 2022 Assembly elections, the BJP won two seats and the SAD three in the 117-member House.
Before the split, the two parties had a seat-sharing arrangement under which the SAD contested 94 Assembly seats and the BJP 23. In Lok Sabha elections, the SAD contested 10 seats and the BJP the remaining three.

title: WhatsApp Web sessions on public computers could expose accounts to cybercriminals, warns Centre
description: India's I4C warned that leaving WhatsApp Web logged in on public computers enables cyberattacks, urging users to manually log out, avoid sensitive chats, and ignore untrusted shared devices to prevent fraud.
author: Onmanorama Staff
content:
WhatsApp Web sessions on public computers could expose accounts to cybercriminals, warns Centre
Mail This Article
New Delhi: Leaving a WhatsApp Web account logged in on a public computer or shared device could expose users to cyberattacks, allowing criminals to access private conversations, impersonate account holders and carry out online fraud, the Centre has warned.
In a recent advisory, the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) under the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), the Union Home Ministry's cybercrime wing, cautioned users against leaving authenticated WhatsApp Web sessions active on computers that could be accessed by others.
Cybercriminals could exploit such sessions to gain unauthorised access to WhatsApp accounts, read private messages, send messages posing as the account holder, and access contact lists and group conversations.
The advisory warned that criminals could misuse the trust associated with a person's identity to launch phishing attempts, social engineering attacks and financial fraud.
Simply closing the browser is not enough
The I4C pointed out that closing a browser tab or window does not necessarily terminate an authenticated WhatsApp Web session. Users must manually log out of their accounts after every session to prevent unauthorised access.
It advised people to exercise particular caution while accessing WhatsApp Web on office computers, shared systems, public computers and devices that may be accessible to others.
The agency also recommended avoiding the exchange of government, organisational, financial, confidential or other sensitive information through WhatsApp Web sessions on computers.
How to stay safe while using WhatsApp Web
The advisory suggested using incognito or private browsing mode when accessing WhatsApp Web is unavoidable. However, users were also cautioned against logging in from untrusted devices, including computers at cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres and borrowed systems.
Users should remain alert to unusual account activity, such as unexpected messages sent from their accounts, unexplained replies from contacts or other suspicious activity.
The I4C also stressed the importance of keeping devices, operating systems and browsers secure and updating security software regularly.
It further advised users to avoid suspicious downloads, unknown files and cracked software that could compromise device security.
(With PTI inputs)

title: Stand-up comedian makes vulgar remark about Bihari women wearing 'sindoor' during Chhath, Congress leader Singvi urges govt to act
description: Comedian mocked Bihari women's Chhath sindoor, sparking outrage. Leaders demanded FIRs. His apology without naming Chhath failed to calm anger.
author: Anshika Pandey
content:
INDIA
Comedian mocked Bihari women's Chhath sindoor, sparking outrage. Leaders demanded FIRs. His apology without naming Chhath failed to calm anger.
Stand-up comedian Yash Maheshwari is facing huge backlash for making vulgar jokes about Bihari women's sindoor tradition during Chhath. Even after his apology, people are demanding FIRs against him in every district of Bihar.
On November 21, Maheshwari posted a stand-up video titled "Morally Questionable | Standup Comedy" to his YouTube page. He made fun of the custom of Bihari ladies wearing long orange sindoor during Chhath in the video. He made a comparison between male genitalia and the length of the sindoor. He inquired why someone was wandering about his home looking like Lord Hanuman and compared women wearing sindoor to the god. In another video, he claimed that Haryanvi men should marry Bihari women since the latter enjoyed beating women and the former enjoyed being battered.
During Chhath, married women pray for their husbands' well-being by applying orange sindoor from their nose to their hair parting. A video related to this tradition sparked significant outrage on social media, with many accusing the creator of insulting Bihar's women, culture, and religious faith, despite laughter from the live audience.
Bihar BJP leader Ritu Jaiswal demanded FIRs against Maheshwari in every district of Bihar, saying attacks on Chhath faith won't be tolerated. Congress leader Abhishek Manu Singhvi also urged Bihar and Delhi Police to register cases. Supreme Court advocate Amita Sachdeva sent him a legal notice with 24 hours to comply, saying respect for faith and women's dignity is non-negotiable.
On November 24 evening, Maheshwari posted a 93-second apology on YouTube, saying he did not intend to hurt religious sentiments and it was 100% his mistake. But he did not mention Chhath, sindoor or Bihari women even once. He has also deactivated his Instagram. Many users said the apology is not enough and questioned Bihar Police's silence. The debate on the limits of comedy has started again.

title: Taliban's Justice In India? Murder accused's hand chopped off with machete, shot down outside court
description: A murder accused, Mandar Maruti Kivle, was attacked with a machete and shot at outside a Pune court while appearing for legal proceedings, just four days after his release from prison.
author: Manisha Chauhan
content:
INDIA
A murder accused, Mandar Maruti Kivle, was attacked with a machete and shot at outside a Pune court while appearing for legal proceedings, just four days after his release from prison.
A man facing a murder case was brutally attacked outside a court in Pune on Wednesday while he had arrived for legal proceedings. The attackers allegedly struck him repeatedly with a machete before shooting at him.
The victim was identified as Mandar Maruti Kivle. Videos of the incident showed two men assaulting him with a machete as he struggled to escape.
Attackers flee on two scooters
After the assault, the two attackers were seen fleeing from the spot on separate scooters. Despite suffering serious injuries, Kivle was seen getting up and attempting to walk away. Subsequent videos showed him lying on a footpath with one of his hands reportedly chopped off.
Bystanders gathered around him as he lay bleeding. His condition and whether he survived the attack were not immediately known.
Victim was jailed in 2025 murder case
According to police, Kivle had been arrested for the murder of Shubham Subhash Chavan in April 2025. Chavan was killed in Pune's Santoshnagar-Katraj area following a dispute involving land and money, police said.
Kivle had been released from prison just four days before the attack. He was targeted outside the court when he arrived for the scheduled legal proceedings.

title: Mumbai local train horror: Man slashes himself with blade after passengers try to wake him | VIDEO
description: Passengers panicked aboard a Nalasopara-Dadar local train after a man allegedly pulled out a blade hidden in his hair and injured himself when they tried to wake him in the handicapped compartment.
author: Manisha Chauhan
content:
MUMBAI
Passengers panicked aboard a Nalasopara-Dadar local train after a man allegedly pulled out a blade hidden in his hair and injured himself when they tried to wake him in the handicapped compartment.
A man allegedly injured himself with a blade inside the handicapped compartment of a Nalasopara-Dadar local train, triggering panic among passengers.
The incident reportedly began when commuters noticed the man sleeping inside the compartment and tried to wake him up. Instead of responding normally, he allegedly began shouting and pulled out a blade that he had hidden in his hair.
Passengers terrified as man attacks himself
The man then allegedly started attacking himself with the blade, sustaining injuries that left him bleeding. The sudden outburst frightened passengers, while the situation inside the compartment quickly turned chaotic.
The incident caused panic among commuters travelling on the local train.

title: 'Should Have Avoided': Cong On SP Declaring List of 5 Candidates for UP Polls
description: The Congress on Wednesday expressed displeasure over the SP announcing a list of five candidates for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls and said this should have been avoided when seat-sharing talks were ongoing.
author: PTI
content:
'Should Have Avoided': Cong On SP Declaring List of 5 Candidates for UP Polls
The Congress on Wednesday expressed displeasure over the SP announcing a list of five candidates for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls and said this should have been avoided when seat-sharing talks were ongoing.
Hours after the second round of the meeting between Congress and the SP on Tuesday, the SP announced its list of five candidates for the elections.
AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors
Asked about the development, AICC in-charge of UP Rajendra Pal Gautam said, "They should have avoided that and waited (for the talks to be over). Nevertheless, this had also happened in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, and some candidates were withdrawn as well." "I hope everything will go in the right direction," Gautam added. On some SP leaders' remarks that the Congress was offered 26 seats, Gautam said, "We don't agree with such statements.
Talks were held after that in a cordial atmosphere. We are holding discussions on all 403 seats." Many seats have been covered in discussions, and the remaining will be done in the next meeting, he told PTI Videos. "So I don't want to say anything. When responsible party leadership is holding discussions, we should be aware of that responsibility and also behave in a responsible manner," Gautam said. His remarks came after Congress MP Imran Masood lashed out at the SP for declaring seats.
"We aren't begging", Congress Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee chief Masood said after the Samajwadi Party announced candidates for five seats. The five seats include one in Saharanpur, Masood's Lok Sabha constituency. The Congress leader said he will discuss with the party leadership whether seat-sharing talks with the SP should continue. "When you are holding talks on one hand and making announcements on the other, it shows that you are not serious," Masood said.
"We will discuss within our party what needs to be done and whether we should sit for talks or not. The party will decide what course of action to take," he told PTI Videos. Questioning the intention of their ally, Masood said, "I do not understand whether you want to fight me, the Congress or the BJP. It needs to be decided whether we want to fight the BJP or fight among ourselves."
Of the five seats that the SP declared candidates for in a surprise move, four are held by its sitting MLAs -- Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana, Umar Ali Khan from Behat and Mehboob Ali from Amroha.
The four seats are in western Uttar Pradesh, where the SP expects a challenge from BJP, its ally RLD, as well as the recently floated Samajik Parivartan Morcha of AIMIM leader Asaduddin Owaisi and Aazad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) chief Chandrashekar Aazad.
Its fifth candidate is Jyoti Lodhi, who will contest from Lalitpur in Bundelkhand. Tej Narain Pandey alias Pawan Pandey was declared the party candidate from Ayodhya in August. Amid the ongoing seat-sharing negotiations for the Uttar Pradesh polls, Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday urged the Congress to focus on "winning equations" rather than the number of seats so that an alliance government could be formed in the state while paving the way for a change at the Centre.
Yadav's remarks in a post in Hindi on X came after discussions between the two parties remained inconclusive for the second consecutive day. Leaders of both parties, however, described the talks as positive and expressed hope that the alliance would be finalised over the next two meetings. Yadav urged the Congress to provide a list of all potential seats they are interested in beyond the 26 seats already proposed by his party. He suggested that based on this, both parties could jointly determine which candidate from either side was best positioned to win a particular seat.
In his message to the Congress on X, the SP chief said, "We will achieve this through harmony and wisdom. With this hope, let us focus on 'winning equations' rather than just seat numbers so that we may win, form our government in UP, and subsequently in Delhi, ensuring that our contribution toward shaping the nation's future is etched in golden letters forever." While the SP offered 26 seats and the Congress handed a list of about 130 seats. Tuesday's meeting in Delhi saw leaders from both parties hold deliberations seat-by-seat. The meeting on Tuesday was attended by Gautam, Aradhana Misra-Mona, Masood and Virendra Chaudhary.
Representing the SP were Ram Gopal Yadav, Shyam Lal Pal, Rajiv Rai, Awadhesh Prasad and Iqra Hasan. The Uttar Pradesh assembly elections are expected to be held in February-March next year. The BJP has won two back-to-back terms in the state since 2017, an outcome the SP is desperate to change this time. The SP and the Congress fought the 2022 elections independently. The two contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections together as part of the opposition INDIA bloc, and the alliance won 43 of the state's 80 seats.

title: Rahul Gandhi's Disproportionate Assets Case: Supreme Court Sends Matter Back To Allahabad HC
description: Supreme Court sets aside Allahabad High Court orders on alleged disproportionate assets against Rahul Gandhi and directs a fresh hearing with the Congress leader included as a respondent.
author: Swastika Sruti
content:
Rahul Gandhi's Disproportionate Assets Case: Supreme Court Sends Matter Back To Allahabad HC
In its ruling today, the Supreme Court overturned the Allahabad High Court's order for investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) against the allegation of possession of disproportionate assets against Congress leader and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi.
AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors
The three-judge bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana remanded the case back to the Allahabad High Court for reconsideration.
The Supreme Court also ordered the petitioner S Vignesh Shishir, a BJP worker, to add Rahul Gandhi as a party respondent in the case and provide him a chance to make submissions in the matter, including about the maintainability of the petition.
It was noted by the Supreme Court that all legal submissions made by the parties in the case would still be open for consideration in the proceedings from scratch.
Supreme Court Says Rahul Gandhi Must Be Heard Before Further Proceedings
Setting aside the earlier orders, the Supreme Court directed that the matter be placed before the Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court to constitute a fresh Bench.
The new Bench will hear the case afresh in an open court. The order also specifically stated that Gandhi must be included as a respondent in the petition.
The Supreme Court observed that Rahul Gandhi should be given an opportunity to respond to the question of maintainability of the writ petition before the High Court proceeds further.
Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal appeared on behalf of Gandhi.
The Congress leader had challenged the Allahabad High Court's directions before the Supreme Court, arguing that the petitioner had no legal standing to seek such an investigation and had not properly disclosed his credentials.
Gandhi also questioned how details of confidential proceedings had appeared in newspaper reports.
How The Disproportionate Assets Case Reached The Supreme Court
This controversy started when S Vignesh Shishir, an activist of BJP, filed a petition alleging disproportionate assets against Rahul Gandhi and other members of his family.
In May, the Allahabad High Court ordered the CBI and ED to verify the allegation raised in the petition.
Later, the High Court asked the CBI to file a fresh affidavit regarding the progress made in the investigation. But the Bench was dissatisfied with the reply provided by the CBI.
According to the directions of the High Court in its order dated July 20, the affidavit provided by the CBI did not satisfy the previous directions and it failed to make the High Court understand the progress made in the investigation.
The High Court further stated that the ED had taken all the necessary steps and it could go ahead with its investigation if it finds anything substantial in it.
Subsequently, Rahul Gandhi moved the Supreme Court contesting the directions issued by the High Court.
Supreme Court Had Earlier Questioned High Court Proceedings
In a previous hearing on August 17, the Supreme Court had expressed its concern over the Allahabad High Court ordering anything without letting Rahul Gandhi defend himself.
The apex court wanted to know as to why orders were being passed pertaining to the Congress leader without hearing him. It further directed the High Court to hold back the proceeding on the matter.
In another move on Wednesday, the Supreme Court proceeded ahead and struck down the orders of the High Court, remanding the matter to be heard afresh.
The fresh hearing will consider the petition along with the objections, if any, of the parties concerned before proceeding further.
Separate Citizenship Allegations Case Against Rahul Gandhi
Meanwhile, another petition filed by S Vignesh Shishir remains pending before the Allahabad High Court. In that matter, the petitioner has sought criminal action against Rahul Gandhi, alleging violations of Indian citizenship laws.
Shishir has claimed that Gandhi held a British passport in addition to his Indian passport.
The High Court had initially ordered the registration of an FIR against Gandhi in this case. However, the judge later withheld the order and recused himself from the matter after the petitioner made certain posts on social media concerning the proceedings.
That case remains separate from the disproportionate assets matter and is still pending before the Allahabad High Court.

title: CJP's Saurav Das Moves Court After Being Stopped At Delhi Airport From Boarding London Flight
description: CJP co-convenor Saurav Das moves Delhi High Court after alleging he was stopped from boarding a London-bound flight over discrepancies in his passport details.
author: Madhuri Adnal
content:
CJP's Saurav Das Moves Court After Being Stopped At Delhi Airport From Boarding London Flight
Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das has moved the Delhi High Court after alleging that he was stopped from travelling to London for an event at the University of Oxford. His lawyer requested an urgent hearing on Wednesday, but the court said it would hear the matter on Thursday.
The plea was mentioned before Acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma. Advocate Krishnaraj Bapat filed the petition, which senior advocate Akhil Sibal will argue before the court on Thursday.
AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors
Das said he was at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport to board his London-bound flight when immigration officials stopped him. He was due to speak at the University of Oxford about the "Cockroach Movement".
According to Das, officials asked him to check a show-cause notice issued by the authorities over differences in the place of birth mentioned in his passport details. He alleged that the notice reached him barely five hours before his flight was scheduled to leave.
The notice reportedly gave him seven days to explain the discrepancy and asked why his passport should not be impounded. Das has claimed that the notice was used to stop him from travelling to the UK.
He has described the incident as an attempt to target and intimidate him, as well as young people associated with the movement. The government has not issued a public response to his allegations so far.
Das also claimed that, besides the Oxford event, students had invited him to speak at the London School of Economics, the University of Cambridge and the University of Edinburgh.

title: Inflation: How rising food prices are squeezing Indian households
description: India's food inflation is broadening, squeezing household budgets.
author: Soutik Biswas
content:
The rising cost of putting food on the table in India
- Published
India's inflation is rising again. And the biggest worry is what's happening to food prices.
The latest government data, external shows retail inflation climbed to 6.09% in October, up from 5.54% in September.
But look more closely at food inflation. It has surged to 8.94%.
The squeeze was sharper in rural India, where food inflation was 9.09%, compared with 8.68% in urban areas.
In other words, food prices are rising considerably faster than the overall rate of inflation.
Food inflation this year has been driven by a combination of weather disruptions, supply shortages and rising input costs, say economists.
With nearly 60% of its farmland dependent on rainfall, external, India remains acutely vulnerable to the vagaries of the monsoon. This year, the southwest monsoon was 13% below normal and unevenly distributed, while intensifying El Niño conditions have heightened risks to farm production.
A survey by polling agency LocalCircles found that six in 10 consumers say household essentials cost them over 20% more each month than a year ago, prompting calls for government intervention.
Rising prices are also forcing cutbacks: 74% are curbing discretionary spending on eating out, shopping and entertainment, while half are buying smaller quantities of essentials.
Food accounts for a smaller share of Indian household spending than it once did, but remains the biggest driver of inflation, with significant economic, social and political consequences.
In India's latest consumer price index, food and beverages account for 36.75% of the basket of goods and services used to measure inflation.
That is down sharply from 45.86% under the previous series, reflecting changing consumption patterns as Indians spend more on services, transport, healthcare, education and other non-food items.
Yet a sharp increase in food prices can move the overall inflation rate significantly, while disproportionately affecting people whose incomes leave little room for adjustment.
"Adjustability for a poor country like India is significantly lower," says Rajeswari Sengupta, an associate professor of economics at Mumbai-based Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research, pointing to the fact that a substantial proportion of household income is still spent on food.
The numbers bear this out.
According to calculations by Dharmakirti Joshi, chief economist at analytics firm Crisil, the bottom 20% of rural households faced inflation of 6.9% in October, against 6.5% for the richest 20%.
In urban India, the corresponding rates were 6.1% and 5.3%.
The pressure is visible even in the cost of a simple meal.
Crisil's Roti Rice Rate analysis, external found that the cost of a home-cooked vegetarian thali - a meal platter - rose 12% year-on-year in October, driven by higher prices of onions, tomatoes, vegetables, edible oil, rice and cooking gas. A non-vegetarian thali became 9% more expensive.
Rice prices were up about 10% year-on-year, pulses 8%, edible oil 13% and LPG 10%, according to Pushan Sharma, director of intelligence at Crisil. "It's no longer a few commodities that are driving this increase, it's becoming a little more broad-based," he says.
When onion prices spike, households can cut back on their consumption to some extent. But substituting rice, pulses and cooking oil is considerably harder.
And food inflation is not just about what farmers produce. It is also about how efficiently that food is stored, processed and moved to the market. Weaknesses at each stage can turn seasonal shortages into sharp price spikes - and gluts into waste.
Onions, for instance, are particularly susceptible to seasonal price swings.
The rabi crop - winter crops, sown after the monsoon and harvested in spring - which accounts for roughly two-thirds of onion production, is harvested in March and April and stored for several months. As stocks dwindle, prices can rise sharply before the next crop arrives.
Tomatoes, meanwhile, tend to see price spikes during the summer months, when arrivals decline in some markets or heat stress affects production.
Sharma says perishables are often responsible for the sudden spikes in food inflation, while prices of staples such as rice and wheat tend to rise more gradually but can stay higher for longer.
"The perishables are what caused the volatility. The non-perishables, like rice and wheat, are the ones that structurally increase the cost," he says.
Economists say India still lacks adequate infrastructure to sort, grade, store and process much of its perishable produce.
Tomatoes, for example, can become so abundant during a glut that farmers struggle to sell them at remunerative prices, only for consumers to face sharply higher prices months later.
Better storage and processing could help turn some of that surplus into products such as puree, smoothing the extremes between abundance and scarcity, according to Sharma
There are other pressures.
Energy shocks feed into the cost of transport, irrigation and agricultural inputs. Fertiliser prices can rise. Global edible-oil markets matter because India relies heavily on imports.
To be true, India, however, has some protection against the worst effects of food inflation.
Government stocks of cereals are comfortably above prescribed minimum levels, and the free-food programme covering nearly 800 million people offers a cushion against rising prices. Rice stocks, external are particularly ample.
There is a wider economic risk, says Sengupta.
"Food inflation may begin with a supply shock, but its effects can spread. Workers who find that their wages no longer cover basic living costs may seek higher pay. Businesses facing higher labour costs may raise prices. What begins as a rise in the price of food can gradually become a more general inflationary pressure - the familiar wage-price spiral that central banks try to prevent," she says.
For India, this creates a particularly difficult balancing act.
Agriculture is a relatively low-productivity sector, and the government has long sought to protect farmers by setting minimum support prices (MSPs) for certain crops - a price floor at which it promises to buy produce, helping farmers guard against a market crash.
At the same time, food prices are politically sensitive. Sharp increases in the price of staples such as onions and tomatoes can quickly anger consumers, prompting governments to step in with measures such as restricting exports, limiting how much traders can stockpile, or otherwise trying to bring prices down.
The broader story of India's changing food consumption makes the current inflation more interesting.
Households are eating differently from a decade ago. An analysis, external of the 2011-12 and 2023-24 consumption surveys shows that the share of cereals in food spending has fallen sharply, particularly among the poorest households, reflecting the impact of subsidised food programmes.
Meanwhile, consumption of nutrient-rich foods such as dairy, fruit and meat has increased across income groups, with the biggest gains among the poorest, the study revealed.
India's food basket is becoming more diverse. But diversity is meaningful only if ordinary Indians can afford it. Ultimately, food inflation is about what makes it to the plate - and what has to be left out.

title: US preparing to unveil plan for new tariffs on global trading partners
description: The new levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, including China and the EU.
author: Jonathan Josephs, Osmond Chia
content:
US preparing to unveil plan for new tariffs on global trading partners
- Published
The US is preparing to announce plans for new tariffs on several countries as early as Wednesday, the BBC understands.
The new import taxes would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, with China, the European Union and Japan among at least 14 jurisdictions affected.
The move comes after the White House's so-called "Section 301" investigation. It was launched in March after the US Supreme Court ruled that President Donald Trump's Liberation Day tariffs were illegal.
Trump has made tariffs a signature policy of his presidency, arguing that they will help boost American manufacturing and create jobs.
The president sent shockwaves around the world when he unveiled sweeping tariffs on global trading partners in April 2025 shortly after his return to the White House.
While the tariffs were later struck down, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer argued then that overproduction abroad was displacing American manufacturing and deterring investment.
Under the new tariffs, countries will face different import tax rates depending on the deals that they have previously struck with Trump.
The announcement is likely to increase tensions between the US and China, the world's two biggest economies, which remain locked in a trade dispute.
Despite last week's meeting between Trump and President Xi Jinping, the two sides have yet to fully resolve their difference with an interim agreement set to expire on 10 January.
In the run up to the Shenzhen summit, the US accused China of not fully living up to the terms of what it agreed in October 2025.
Washington said Beijing was falling short on its commitments, "particularly as they relate to agricultural purchases, rare earths, and other critical minerals".
However earlier on Tuesday China extended the suspension of a ban on exports critical minerals including gallium, germanium, antimony until 27 January. The ban would otherwise have come into force on Friday.
The Trump administration's tariff policy has been criticised for putting up prices for American consumers and damaging the global economy.
  - Published22 August

title: Bangladesh's ex-PM Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return on 16 December
description: Hasina has spoken several times of her desire to return, but this is the first time she has set a date.
author: Zoya Mateen
content:
Bangladesh's ex-PM Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return on 16 December
- Published
Bangladesh's former prime minister Sheikh Hasina has said she plans to return home on 16 December, more than two years after a popular uprising forced her from power.
Hasina, who has lived in exile in Delhi since August 2024, has asked the Bangladeshi government to fly her back to Dhaka, her spokesperson said.
The announcement comes amid renewed unrest in Bangladesh, where supporters of her Awami League party have staged protests despite a ban on its activities.
But it's unclear how Hasina will return. Last year, a Bangladeshi court sentenced her to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown on student-led protests that ended her 15-year rule. She denies the charges.
Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Humayun Kabir dismissed the prospect of Hasina returning on her own terms.
"Sheikh Hasina will not be able to return to the country as an ordinary commercial passenger; she will be brought back in handcuffs," he told a press briefing on Tuesday.
Kabir also accused Hasina and Delhi of fomenting recent unrest in Bangladesh, alleging that they were backing "terrorist activities" in the country.
India's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In April, the ministry said it was examining Bangladesh's request to extradite her and that it wanted to "engage constructively with the new government and further strengthen bilateral ties".
Hasina fled to India on 5 August 2024 as tens of thousands of protesters descended on Dhaka, and crowds stormed her official residence.
What began as student protests against quotas in government jobs turned into a mass uprising against her government following a deadly crackdown on demonstrators. The UN estimates that up to 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.
On Tuesday, Hasina's spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali accused Bangladeshi authorities of forcing her into exile in violation of the country's constitution.
"Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on 5 August 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," he said in a statement.
The choice of date is significant. Bangladesh celebrates Victory Day on 16 December, marking the end of its 1971 war of independence from Pakistan. Hasina's father, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, led the country's independence movement.
Abu Obaidha Arin, an aide to Hasina, described her decision as "deeply symbolic". "We firmly believe that she will celebrate this historic day among her people," he said, expressing confidence that she would once again lead Bangladesh.
Hasina's announcement - and Dhaka's sharp response to it - come at a time when the ousted leader is seeking to reassert her political relevance from exile.
The Awami League was banned from political activities in May last year under the interim government led by Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus, which took charge after Hasina's ouster.
The party was subsequently barred from contesting February's general election, which brought its long-time rival, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), to power, with Tarique Rahman becoming prime minister.
But the ban has not put an end to street protests by Awami League supporters, who have also called for nationwide shutdowns demanding Hasina's return.
Hasina, meanwhile, has repeatedly spoken of her desire to return to Bangladesh, even as she has acknowledged the risks of doing so.
"I know that they may put me in jail or they may kill me, anything may happen, but still I have to go back," she told a gathering of journalists in Delhi over an audio link in August, on the second anniversary of her ouster.
Hasina's continued political activities from Indian soil have also complicated Delhi's efforts to rebuild ties with Dhaka.
India enjoyed close relations with Hasina during her 15 years in power and had hoped that the election of a new government in Bangladesh would offer an opportunity to reset ties, which deteriorated sharply after her ouster.
But nine months after taking office, Rahman is yet to visit India despite an invitation. He has travelled to China, Japan and Malaysia, and skipped the BRICS summit hosted by India in September.
Discussions over a possible visit in August coincided with anger in Dhaka over Hasina's remarks to journalists in Delhi.
The two countries have since resumed talks about a visit, but no dates have been announced.

title: Exclusive: China-Pakistan satellite waltz is watching every inch of India 24×7
description: This is the third exclusive by ThePrint on China's satellite surveillance of India.
author: Soumya Pillai
content:
New Delhi: China and Pakistan are building a coordinated network of satellites that could provide persistent surveillance of Indian territory. This space-based cooperation was consolidated during the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, a space surveillance report highlights.
According to a report by Bengaluru-based space surveillance startup Digantara, exclusively accessed by ThePrint, Chinese space capabilities, including satellite data, may have been used to observe Indian military installations and other strategic sites during Operation Sindoor.
One of the most significant findings points to the role of China’s high-resolution optical remote-sensing satellite, Yaogan-41, during the 88-hour military confrontation between India and Pakistan.
“Chinese Satellite Yaogan-41 offers continuous subcontinent coverage. A dual-use satellite, it tracked Indian airbases during Operation Sindoor,” the report read.
While the report pointed to the specific use of Yaogan-41 against India during Operation Sindoor, it also explained how China and Pakistan have been building a complementary network of space surveillance to ensure that not an inch of India is left unmonitored.
Between January 2025 and June 2026, Pakistan placed six satellites in orbit. Five of these—Pakistan Remote Sensing Satellite-Earth Observation 1 (PRSC-EO1), Pakistan Remote Sensing Satellite-2 (PRSS-2), HS-1, PRSC-EO2 and PRSC-EO3—were launched on Chinese rockets, in Chinese launch facilities. While all these satellites are individually placed to focus on Indian territory, they also complement the Chinese network of satellites.
The combined Earth-observation capabilities of the Pakistani and Chinese satellites give a more continuous picture of Indian military infrastructure, troop movements, border installations, airbases, naval facilities and strategic assets.
“China launched five satellites for Pakistan, enhancing ISTAR and observation of Indian assets and space monitoring capabilities,” the report read.
ISTAR is a military system that combines information gathered from satellites, drones, aircraft, radars, ground sensors and intelligence networks to give a military force a detailed picture of its adversary’s activities and capabilities.
Experts suggested that with China sharpening its space ambitions, India will need to work on its capabilities to increase its presence in space.
The Pak satellites
The Digantara report showed that the China-supported Pakistani space launches began much before 2025. Starting in 2018, satellites including PRSC-EO1, PakSat MM1, ICUBE-Q, PRSS-1 and Pak TES 1A were already eyeing Indian territory, placed in orbits complementing the existing Chinese network of satellites.
The meticulously choreographed satellite network waltz, when viewed as a whole, is designed so that as one satellite moves out of range of a particular region, another moves into position to take over, ensuring consistent coverage of the area. These Pakistani satellites are, in a way, filling the small gaps left in the already expansive Chinese satellite network. The orbits for these satellites are also chosen to ensure that regions of interest are monitored from multiple angles, range and clarity.
For instance, the PRSS-1 is Pakistan’s Earth-observation satellite, launched alongside PakTES-1A in July 2018. It is an electro-optical imaging payload, with two principal image products—panchromatic and multispectral.
Panchromatic imagery can distinguish objects or features roughly one metre across under suitable imaging conditions. Multispectral imagery captures information across different portions of the electromagnetic spectrum, helping identify vegetation, land-use patterns, water bodies and other surface features.
According to the Pakistani space agency, Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO), PRSS-1 offers a four-day revisit capability anywhere on the globe. For example, if PRSS-1 captures an image of Delhi on Monday, it can capture another image of Delhi approximately four days later. It can do the same for locations elsewhere in the world. This allows scientists and authorities to monitor changes on the ground. PRSS-1 has ground stations in Islamabad and Karachi for receiving, processing, and archiving satellite imagery.
PAKSAT-MM1, launched in 2024, is a communications satellite, developed with Chinese assistance. It is designed to provide telecommunications services across Pakistan and surrounding regions. It carries payloads operating in four frequency bands: C-band for television broadcasting and communications, Ku-band for broadcasting, VSAT (very small aperture terminal) connectivity and mobile backhaul, Ka-band for high-speed broadband and high-throughput internet, and L-band for satellite-based augmentation services (SBAS), which can improve positioning and navigation accuracy.
PRSC-EO1, on the other hand, is a part of Pakistan’s newer remote-sensing satellite programme, which uses optical sensors to acquire images of the Earth’s surface.
All of these satellites received technological and launch support from China.
In 2022, Pakistan’s SUPARCO and the China Great Wall Industry Corporation (CGWIC)—a subsidiary of China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC)—signed a multi-launch service agreement to provide Pakistan with a long-term arrangement to launch multiple satellites using China’s rockets and associated technical services.
Also read: Exclusive: 3 Chinese satellites stayed focused on Gujarat coast during Operation Sindoor
Complementing ground support
Digantara’s space surveillance report has also found Pakistan’s growing involvement in the Asia-Pacific Ground-Based Space Object Observation System Project (APOSOS) to be concerning.
APOSOS is a multinational space-surveillance network initiated under the Asia-Pacific Space Cooperation Organization (APSCO), in which China plays a central role in its operation and data management. The project uses ground-based optical telescopes to observe and track objects in space, including satellites.
Curiously, Pakistan was one of the three countries where the first three observation nodes or stations of APOSOS were established. Each node is equipped with a 15-cm aperture optical telescope, and observation data from the different nodes is transmitted to a central facility at the National Astronomical Observatories of the Chinese Academy of Sciences in China’s capital, Beijing. The other two stations are Peru and Iran.
Since Pakistan is not just a member of APOSOS, but the host of one of the facilities, it has gained a geographical advantage of getting access to observations from different parts of the world, which can be used to track satellites in orbit, including India’s space assets.
This is the third article in ThePrint’s exclusive three-part series examining China’s space surveillance moves.
(Edited by Ratan Priya)

title: BJP mobilises Sri Rama Sene as Karnataka weighs repeal of anti-conversion, cow slaughter laws
description: The Karnataka Protection of Right to Freedom of Religion Act, 2022, and Karnataka Prevention of Slaughter and Preservation of Cattle Act, 2020 was passed by the erstwhile BJP govt.
author: Sharan Poovanna
content:
Bengaluru: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the principal opposition party in Karnataka, met with Sri Ram Sene controversial head Pramod Muthalik to shore up support to oppose the likelihood of D.K. Shivakumar-led government from repealing the anti-cattle slaughter and anti-conversion laws.
Although it is not official yet, the state government has indicated the possibility of repealing the Karnataka Protection of Right to Freedom of Religion Act, 2022, and Karnataka Prevention of Slaughter and Preservation of Cattle Act, 2020 at the winter session of the state legislature in Belagavi.
“I met with Sri Pramod Muthalik, founder of Sri Ram Sene, in Bengaluru today, and we discussed several issues. We held extensive discussions on several matters concerning the protection of the interests of the Hindu community in the state, including the designs of this anti-Hindu Congress government, which is seeking to repeal the law banning cow slaughter,” BJP state chief B.Y. Vijayendra said in a post on X.
Several pro-Hindu groups, including Muthalik-led Sri Ram Sene, Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) and others have also threatened protests if the government attempts to repeal the legislation.
The Congress party, which enjoys the backing of minority groups like Christians and Muslims, is under pressure to repeal the two controversial BJP-era laws.
In October, Christian and Muslim spiritual and community leaders demanded the Congress government fulfil its 2023 poll promises of repealing contentious legislations that targeted specific minority and oppressed communities.
Rev. Peter Machado, the Archbishop of Bengaluru, and Mohammed Yahya Damudi, the convener of the Karnataka Rajya Muslim Okkoota (KRMO), told reporters the ruling party should repeal both the laws as well as the immediate implementation of the proposed Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025.
Shivakumar has been under pressure to make good on the 2023 poll promises that helped the Congress storm to power with a clear majority. However, the Congress government–both under Siddaramaiah and Shivakumar–have not been able to withdraw the two contentious legislations despite the administration enjoying three years in power.
The hate speech Bill was sent from Karnataka’s Lok Bhavan to President Droupadi Murmu for her consideration on the grounds that the Bill was flawed. All three bills were passed by the previous BJP government between 2019 and 2022.
The Congress had earlier claimed that it lacked a clear majority in the Upper House of the state legislature which impeded the smooth passage or withdrawal of bills. In October, the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) managed to retain three and wrest control of another MLC seat in the elections.
The Congress now has 37 members in the Karnataka Legislative Council as against 24 of the BJP and seven of the Janata Dal (Secular). There are five vacant seats and one Independent in the 75-member house. By this count, the NDA has 31 seats in total.
Despite the party-wise tally, minority groups have intensified their demands seeking a repeal of the contentious laws as delays have been adding to the brewing discontentment among the core support base of the Congress.
This includes anger from the Muslim community over the denial of MLA tickets in the Davangere by-elections and follow-up action against two prominent community leaders, including the removal of Nasser Ahmed as the chief minister’s political secretary.
(Edited by Tony Rai)

title: 22-yr-old held in Meerut for ‘plotting’ attack on armed forces, a year after associate’s Jammu arrest
description: A member of several social media groups propagating terror acts run by Pakistani radicals, Uzaid quit NEET preparation to plan suicide attack, indoctrinate adolescents
author: Mayank Kumar
content:
New Delhi: The Uttar Pradesh Police has arrested a resident of Meerut for allegedly being part of a terror conspiracy to carry out a fidayeen (suicide) attack at an Army camp or a convoy of the armed forces.
Identified as Uzaid, the 22-year-old accused was found to be a member of several social media groups run by Pakistan-based handlers that feature radicalisation and propagation of terrorist acts, Meerut Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) B.B.G.T.S. Murti said in a statement Tuesday.
“The role of the accused came to light based on allegations regarding his association with radical and anti-India content on social media, his contact with suspicious individuals linked to Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), his active participation in groups operating on encrypted platforms, and his involvement in promoting anti-national activities,” the SSP said.
Uzaid, according to him, had “propagated ideas aimed at targeting the political leadership, the military, and police personnel through suicide attacks, and to have incited adolescents—those over the age of 14—to engage in terrorist activities, and jihad”.
पाकिस्तान से जुड़े शहजाद भट्टी एवं संदिग्ध व्यक्तियों द्वारा संचालित सोशल मीडिया ग्रुपों के माध्यम से राष्ट्रविरोधी गतिविधियों के संबंध में थाना कोतवाली पुलिस एवं स्वाट टीम नगर द्वारा आतंकवाद से जुड़े ऑनलाइन मॉड्यूल का खुलासा एवं 01 अभियुक्त उजैद गिरफ्तार।#UPPolice #MeerutPolice pic.twitter.com/0LoHPRttFR
— MEERUT POLICE (@meerutpolice) November 24, 2026
His arrest in Meerut comes months after a team of the Jammu police raided a location in the vicinity looking for him. Sources privy to the probe said there were discrepancies in the accused’s name. “The Jammu Police had inputs and digital data suggesting the name of the accused was Sadik, who operated the handler account ‘Ibneaadam99’. The verification was not successful earlier,” a police source said.
The Anti-Terrorism Squad and Intelligence Bureau have questioned Uzaid about the extent of his presence on anti-India social media channels and groups.
He came under the radar of the police and intelligence agencies after the Jammu police arrested a local student, Mohammed Sajid, in November 2025, and a scrutiny of his phone revealed “highly incriminating materials”, including suspicious chats on Session and WhatsApp as well as several Instagram handles.
The Internet Protocol (IP) addresses of two of the five Instagram IDs uncovered by the police—’drvgsjih4di’ and ‘abumusablhafs’—were traced to the Prime broadband service in Pakistan’s Multan. According to the police, when Sajid joined this Instagram community, he was preparing for the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (Undergraduate), or NEET (Undergraduate), attending a prominent coaching class in Jammu.
Radicalisation by Pakistan-based handlers, however, led him to abandon NEET coaching, isolate himself, and secretly engage with extremist associates, they said. From Instagram, where they were running a group named ‘Al-Mujahid’, which was subsequently renamed ‘Tuition’ for concealment, they shifted to Session App under the group name ‘005brigade’.
After his arrest, Uzaid allegedly revealed to the police the specific code words for their planned attack—‘intezam’ for logistics, ‘shahadat’ for martyrdom, and ‘jacket’ for a suicide jacket.
During the probe, the Jammu police received information regarding four suspicious Instagram IDs: Ibneaadam99 (Meerut), Kamran_07865 (Kishtwar), Drugsjihadi_ (Pakistan), and Abumusablhafs (Pakistan), the Meerut SSP said, adding that the first one was allegedly linked to Uzaid in Meerut.
Murti added that Uzaid came into contact with Sajid after the former commented ‘we are also ready’ on one of the several anti-India videos he watched on Instagram, YouTube.
According to the inputs, Uzaid played a key role in managing these groups and maintained contact with Sajid via Instagram, Session, and Signal. As part of the module, two more groups, named ‘Tuition-40’ and ‘Brigade’, were created on Instagram and the Session app, which had individuals such as Amir Hamza (PoK), Abu Musab (Punjab, Pakistan), Furkan (PoK), Kamran, and other suspicious persons as members.
Further, the Meerut SSP said Uzaid was associated with several religious gatherings and groups since 2023 and used to download inflammatory audio clips and share with teens to recruit and incite for terrorist activities and ‘jihad,’ deleting the files later.
“Interrogation further revealed that Uzaid and his associates planned a fidayeen (suicide) attack for November 2025, targeting a major Army camp or an Army convoy,” the Meerut SSP said. “Sajid was tasked with conducting reconnaissance, while Uzaid was assigned the responsibility of executing the plot, with the necessary weapons and explosive-laden jackets to be provided to him. It has come to light that these materials and training were to be facilitated via the Gurez Valley.”
He said that Uzaid was also found to be a member of a WhatsApp group which may have links to the Lashkar-e-Taiba, or be connected to social media accounts operated by notorious Pakistani gangster Shahzad Bhatti. “Further verification and investigation into these allegations and the roles of the individuals involved are currently underway.”
(Edited by Nardeep Singh Dahiya)

title: Fact-Check: Viral Video of a Raccoon Protecting Her Babies Is AI-Generated
description: Fact-Check: An AI-generated video is going viral on social media with false claims that it shows a raccoon refusing to leave a flooded car until all her babies are safe and out of danger.
author: Anika K
content:
A video is going viral on social media, claiming to show a raccoon refusing to leave a flooded car until all her babies were safe and out of danger.
- News organisation News9 were among the accounts sharing the video.
How did we find out?: We ran a reverse image search on the video using Google Lens and found a Facebook reel with the same visuals.
- The video is captioned, "Rescue crews battling the Kentucky flood found a mother raccoon on the roof of a sinking car, refusing to leave her three babies… what she did next left the whole crew in tears. Would you have risked it?
- However, the video has an AI tag, added by the user.
- We went through the Facebook page and found out that they have posted several similar AI-generated videos.
- The account bio reads, "Generated videos for fun, surprise and good vibes."
Is the video AI?: We ran the video through Hive Moderation, an AI detector, which flagged it as 98.3 percent likely to have been AI-generated.
- We also ran the video through DeepFake-O-Meter, and three of its detectors flagged the viral clip as AI-generated.
Conclusion: The video is AI-generated and doesn't show real footage of a raccoon protecting her babies.
